Introduction

You may wonder, as do I, and as do people

everywhere: how could this great scholar have gained

access to such truth, when all of the earlier scholars

and the great guides and imams failed to do so? I

would reply to you: a person has nothing except

what they strive for.

Indeed, people are differentiated through their actions.

This is true even for the Envoys (Messengers) and

noble Prophets… and there will be a different level for

everyone according to their deeds in this world.

Our own great scholar Mohammad Emin Sheikho

was given awareness and understanding by Al’lah,

and he was distinguished by his outstanding deeds

and his great and humane sacrifices. Al’lah did not

give him anything except that which he deserved.

God says, “And We sent it down deservedly, and

with righteousness it came down.”

The Dignity of a Believing Officer

e had no other choice but to act as he did; his

wisdom prompted him to demonstrate such a

reaction in order to stave off the dreadful situation

and put an end to the farce instigated by the arrogant

Turkish officer.

A blanket of silence and an awful feeling of terror fell

throughout the whole of government house, for all the

officers and staff were thunderstruck at what they had just

heard. They stood perfectly still, as if frozen to the spot,

and gaped in amazement, hardly able to believe what had

just taken place!

‘Is it possible?’ they all asked themselves, ‘did this really

happen? Oh… how dare he?’ Yes, indeed! In the middle of the

presidential palace, in the actual presence of not only a crowd

of Turkish officers, but also the two most important men in the

country: the governor-general and the commander-in-chief

who were both in the building… the Arab officer, Mohammad

Emin Sheikho, caring nothing for any one of them, brought

out his revolver and shot in the direction of a Turkish officer!

Everyone who saw the event and those who heard the

shooting were overcome by a sense of awe and terror when

H

— صفحة 13 —

Stories of the Scholar

12

faced with this shocking situation. As for the officer whom

Mohammad Emin had aimed at, when he saw the revolver

directed towards him the words of mockery stopped inside

his mouth which was agape due to its owner’s stupefaction.

This quickly turned into dreadful dismay as the sound of

shooting reverberated in his ears. He felt his heart fall to his

boots as the bullet flashed past his ear; with the shock of

this his power faded and his arrogance vanished, while his

heart palpitated strongly and irregularly as though it would

become detached from his body.

Truly, this incident was a great deterrent for him: after

this lesson his spirit would never again dare to suggest that

he should involve himself in troubles with the Arab officer

Aslan, not even with so much as a single derogatory word.

For he found him to be a man who cared for nothing, not

even death, if anything should offend his dignity and pride.

This astonishing event took place when the eminent

scholar was still an officer working in the government

house in Damascus. There, all the officers, senior or junior,

had the greatest respect for this reputable officer because of

his humanity, his distinguished character and high sense of

honour they sensed emanating from him, in addition to the

success of his great feats, the likes of which they knew they

were incapable of achieving. The awe-inspiring demeanour

of our officer caused them to avoid showing or practising

any breach of God’s Orders in his presence.

We shall relate, dear reader, what caused this awful

incident on that particular day. A group of officers were

— صفحة 14 —

The Dignity of a Believing Officer

13

standing in the foyer of the building having a conversation,

and from time to time they burst into raucous laughter.

They were engaged in their vulgar, sexual jokes when

one of them noticed Aslan, the Arab officer, coming

towards them. He hastily turned to the Turkish officer

standing beside him who was still uttering shameful words,

‘Hush! Be careful, don’t say any more now.’

The Turkish officer looked at his friend and saw that his

face had turned deathly pale, so he turned to see who or

what had caused his friend’s confusion.

In the meantime, Officer Sheikho was still walking

towards the main door of the building and approaching the

crowd of officers. The Turkish officer looked at him and

realised that he was an officer equal to him in rank, so he

turned back to his friend and asked in amazement, ‘What’s

wrong with you? I thought you were warning me of the

commander-in-chief! Are you cautioning me about an

officer equal to me in rank?’

‘He’s a sheikh (a religious scholar),’ answered the first

officer who could hardly utter his words for he could see

how close Aslan was to them and could easily hear them.

A bellow of laughter issued from the haughty, conceited

Turkish officer followed by a particularly rude comment

full of scorn as he looked at the Arab officer and mocked

him, ‘Sh… sh..sh… eikh… Ha… ha… ha…! Sh..sh…

shei… kh..kh!’

But no sooner had he finished saying this than the sound

of a shot rang out, sounding as loud as a cannon-shot in the

— صفحة 15 —

Stories of the Scholar

14

large hall of the government house as it resounded like a clap

of thunder on the ears of the uncouth, aggressive officer.

Although the bullet zoomed past his ear and did not scathe

him he felt as though it had hit him and exploded in his

head, so he fell to the floor with his eyes bulging, and

trembling from head to toe with fear and alarm.

The bullet went straight through a wooden wall and

continued on its path to pass between two clerks without

touching them and eventually it settled in the outer wall of

the hall!

Silence prevailed throughout the entire building, for

everybody had either witnessed the event or heard the

thunderous sound, and they stood speechless and motionless,

their hearts fluttering, totally overcome by a state of shock.

Aslan, our high-minded officer, continued unflinchingly

on his way, caring for nothing, until he left the hall and came

to the outer square of the government house. He left them all

behind, lost in a state of shock, the brazen officer still lying flat

on the floor, senseless and seized by violent fear.

The governor-general was in his office with the

commander-in-chief when he heard the shot so, naturally,

he became alarmed and jumped to his feet. He sent the

commander-in-chief to inquire about the matter. The chief

commandant dashed out of the room like a bolt of

lightning and, overwhelmed with anxiety, he asked the

officers in the hall who had fire a gun. Their faces blushed

with embarrassment as the brother officers reluctantly told

their commander that it was Aslan. Without waiting for

— صفحة 16 —

The Dignity of a Believing Officer

15

any further details about the incident the commandant

turned back to the office he had come from and spoke

directly to the governor-general, the ruler of the country.

‘Your Honour! All is well. Some mischievous children

tossed fireworks into the hall, but the gendarmes have

thrown them out.’

When the governor knew that it was only children

playing he calmed down and regained his composure.

Fortunately the commander-in-chief did not ask for any

further explanation of the event nor did he instigate further

inquiries as to what had moved the Arab officer to commit

such a grave, lawless act inside the inviolable house of

government. This is because his friendly relations with

Aslan, his firm trust in the wisdom of this honest officer

and the magnificent measures he consistently took in the

problems and difficulties that faced him in all his duties,

made the commander-in-chief have absolute faith that

there must have been a good reason and motive behind

Aslan’s behaviour and that he had definitely acted in the

most correct and appropriate way.

The commander did not tell the governor that there

really had been a shooting, nor did he even approach the

Arab officer involved. He allowed the serious event to pass

and be forgotten as if nothing had happened.

Truly, the commander had such faith in our officer that

the event of the shooting, despite its gravity, seemed a

frivolous matter when compared to the many glorious

performances of this humane officer.

— صفحة 17 —

Stories of the Scholar

16

It was Al’lah’s Will to defend the faith and dignity of

this humane officer and to maintain him as an honourable,

reverend master at the height of Godly Glory.

Thus, through the devilment of the Turkish officer who

had dared to belittle Officer Sheikho, He raised him above

all the Turkish officers, a matter which made them deem

him a man to be reckoned with even more than before.

They were afraid to misbehave with him, even in jest, due

to their appreciation of his awe-inspiring personality and

high prestige that was imprinted in their hearts.

As for that flippant, ill-mannered officer, he received due

payment for his insolence, and thereafter he never dared to

mention the name of our righteous officer or even look at

his noble face.

This was the proper outcome, for glory belongs only to

God, to His Envoy

1 and to all true believers.

1 The word ‘Envoy’ also means ‘Messenger’.

— صفحة 18 —

17

His Enemies Confessed to His Excellence

hen Mohammad Emin Sheikho, the security

officer, held the post of section manager in al-

Zabadani, he girded his loins and prepared to

work hard to overcome the troubles and strife which

afflicted his country. This caused him no difficulty as he

was accustomed to tackling these matters in a positive and

straightforward manner: by chasing criminals and arresting

them until eventually the whole region capitulated to his

justice.

In this way, the security situation was stabilised and order

restored once again. Peace spread throughout the region and

again people were able to go out of their houses safely and

untroubled, after they had spent a long time being afraid and

concerned. They had feared for their lives because of the

criminal elements that prevailed in that area and the villages

around it. But now, due to the brave deeds of Officer

Sheikho, they were able to leave the safety of their houses in

order to go to work and tend their orchards, with smiles on

their faces.

Indeed, this officer spared no effort and sacrificed a lot of

time along with his soldiers – who were, in fact, repentant

W

— صفحة 19 —

Stories of the Scholar

18

criminals – in order to establish peace and security all over

this region.

The people of the region fully realised all this and saw the

results with their own eyes, for there was now a great

difference in the security of the region between the period

preceding Officer Sheikho taking up this post and the period

that followed it. This is particularly significant when we

know that the Ottoman State had failed to control the

region of which we write, as it was adjacent to Lebanon.

This gave the criminals the opportunity to flee into Lebanon

where they could be protected by the international Law of

the Protectorate which prevented the Ottoman authorities

from having any power inside the Protectorate for any reason

whatsoever.

To show the excellence of his deeds, dear reader, we

should point out that after only one year of Officer Sheikho

holding the post of regional manager, fresh produce and

other goods were flowing freely in to the market once

again, and the normal daily activities of buying and selling

were safely resumed.

It had been many days since the commander had last

visited this region in order to inspect the situation. There

existed a firm relationship between this commander and

Mohammad Emin: a relationship of love and appreciation

which gave the humane officer a special and distinguished

position in the eyes of the commander. In fact, it was a

position that was higher than that of all the other officers

because of his great achievements and unique successes.

— صفحة 20 —

His Enemies Confessed to His Excellence

19

This close relationship meant that they would often visit

one another, especially when Mohammad Emin held a post

away from the government house in the city of Damascus,

where the commander worked.

It had been some time since the last meeting between the

commander and the officer when Mohammad Emin decided

to visit the commander and, as usual, he wanted to take a

gift with him, but what should it be? He decided to take two

baskets of apples, for the apples of this region are the finest

in the world.

The following morning he rushed off to Damascus

taking with him a large quantity of these delicious apples

and, upon his arrival, he went straight to the commander’s

house with a porter carrying the two baskets.

The exemplary master knocked gently at the door and

waited patiently. After a few moments the door was opened

to reveal the commander and what a shock he received! He

had not expected such a visitor on this day and at this time!

He stared at the face of the benevolent master, and after

some moments of silence, he barely managed to stutter a

few words.

‘Ah… welcome… welcome Aslan! May Al’lah’s curse be

on the driver… he dared to put a bottle of wine in the car,

so I accidentally spilt it on my clothes… they’re completely

stained with the wine… wait for me Aslan while I change

them… may Al’lah’s curse be on the driver.’

Officer Mohammad Emin was astonished at the

commander’s behaviour and his manner of talking… he

20

wondered, ‘What’s the matter with him? And why is he

talking in such a feeble, hesitant way? His words seem to be

those of a man who was afraid and ashamed… what a

strange thing!’

He had never known his commander to speak like this

before.

The commander stopped talking and began to move

backwards wanting to go and change his clothes, then Aslan

addressed him with a look of astonishment on his face. ‘But

sir… Commander… I wanted to offer you this,’ he said,

pointing at the two baskets of apples.

‘All right… all right Aslan… thanks… thank you… put

it here inside.’ the commander replied, speaking more

quickly now.

Then he drew back leaving the honest officer standing

there in a state of astonishment… wondering to himself but

finding no logical reason, ‘Why did the commander behave

like that? Why does he appear to be so confused and

afraid?’

It was really very strange: the commander of the Ottoman

army in all the al-Sham countries was shaking and extremely

confused at the sight of one of his officers!

Later, and still in such a state, he returned to his guests,

a group of officers who were gathered in a room of his

house. They too were worried at the sight and of him, and

his sorry state which was obvious from his face and in his

movements. Then they immediately jumped up as though

they had been stung for they thought it was a very serious

— صفحة 22 —

His Enemies Confessed to His Excellence

21

matter. ‘Is it possible that the governor of al-Sham is

coming now? Or what could it be?’

Every one of them made his own analysis of the situation

of their leader, as they had never seen him in such a state

before. They knew him, but always as a man of strong

character and incomparable equanimity and bravery. But

now, what was wrong with him? And who or what might

have caused this situation?

The following day, an important Turkish officer visited

Officer Mohammad Emin and said to him, ‘Aslan! The

commander is certainly afraid of you!’

‘What? He’s afraid of me! But why?’ said Officer

Mohammad Emin.

He told Officer Mohammad Emin what had happened

on the previous day and the reason for the commander’s

strange state, then the conversation that was held between

the commander and his officers after he had appeared totally

confused, as if he had met the Grand Vizier or even the

Ottoman Sultan when they were displeased with him.

One of the visiting officers said, ‘What’s the matter sir…

what’s the matter?’

The commander replied in his confused tone, ‘Aslan…

it’s Aslan.’

When the officers heard this word, their wish to hear the

answer that was tinged with fear, instantly turned to

extreme astonishment, to the extent that many of them

asked at the same moment, ‘What’s the problem with him?’

— صفحة 23 —

Stories of the Scholar

22

The commander answered, ‘Can’t you see how drunk

we are… the smell of wine has spread throughout the

house.’

Some of them answered, ‘Oh commander! Let it be…

what’s the problem… as he’s one of the officers under your

authority?’

The commander replied, ‘That’s true… but he is noble

Aslan… a man of the highest morals… he is an honourable

man… no… no… he isn’t like us at all… we are vile, but

he is pure and chaste.’

With that, all the officers remained silent and bowed

their heads, each one of them remembering what he had

seen or heard about officer Aslan, that venerable, humane

man. Then they agreed that what they had heard from the

commander was, indeed, the very truth. It is true that Aslan

was an officer just as they were, but he was not actually like

them at all. Although they held a higher military rank than

his he soared far above them in the skies of purity and

chastity, and was far superior to them in morals and deeds.

He was, in fact, a most honourable officer with sublime

principles.

At that moment, Officer Mohammad Emin knew the

reason for what he had witnessed the previous day, and the

mystery that had baffled him all during the night was solved.

Thus, the possessor of high morals and sublime principles

is always a master wherever he goes, and due to his

uprightness he is respected by all people. This is because his

— صفحة 24 —

His Enemies Confessed to His Excellence

23

Almighty Lord has clothed him in the garment of dignity

and reverence for he has controlled his spirit and mastered it.

Therefore, all the people around him, whether friends or

enemies, can testify to his noble morals.

The People of Quraysh knew God’s Envoy Mohammad

(cpth)

1 before the Mission as: the true, the honest, possessor

of great morals due to all that they had witnessed of his

uprightness and noble manners. Then Al’lah the Almighty

addressed them indicating his high spiritual state, with the

noble verse, “Your companion has never been misled,

nor has he deviated [from the uprightness].”

2

For it was true that they had never seen him deviate

from the course of virtue and rightness, neither before the

Mission nor after it. God’s Envoy (cpth) had never shaken

hands with a woman or glanced at her illicitly, nor had he

prostrated himself before an idol. If this had not been the

truth, they would have said, ‘The Qur’an has not been

revealed to him, for he has gone astray.’

Similarly, our venerable scholar, Mohammad Emin,

adopted Al’lah’s Path and followed His Guidance truthfully

and ethically: thus he attained all the true knowledge from

Al’lah.

This is the answer to whoever asks the following, ‘From

where did he get his knowledge? And why was it revealed to him

personally and not to another one of the religious scholars?’

1 (cpth) is an acronym for ‘communication with Al’lah and peace are through him.’

2 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 53, The Star (al-Najm), verse 2.

— صفحة 25 —

24

The Officer, a Repentant Criminal

and a Chicken Coop

hen

Officer

Mohammad

Emin

Sheikho

assumed the leadership of the police station in

the districts of al-Midan and al-Shaghour his

daring deeds certainly equalled those he had previously

carried out in the regions of al-Salhiyeh and al-Akrad. He

became the chief topic of conversation of the criminals of

these two quarters since he had destroyed their evil ways. On

the one hand he saved people from the wrongdoing and evil

actions of these criminals,, and on the other he released the

spirits of these criminals from the wrongful intentions settled

therein, which would cause them to lose forever their eternal

life, yet to come, as they would forfeit the donation which

God had prepared for them because of the crimes they

committed against humanity during their mortal lives.

In fact, there is a certain type of men who, in their

distorted point of view, think that true manhood belongs only

to them and that all other men are mere lesser specimens of

manhood. This was the belief of many men during the time

of our officer. They were deceived by the appearance of their

W

— صفحة 26 —

The Officer, a Repentant Criminal and a Chicken Coop

25

huge bodies and taut muscles, not to mention their gruff

voices and overbearing manner of speaking, by which they

thought they displayed heroism and bravado before ordinary,

law-abiding people.

They were so proud of their long twirled moustaches, to

the extent that they might spend a considerable period of

time standing vainly before a mirror, waxing and twirling

them, as proud as peacocks at what was reflected back at

them. Such moustaches were considered the measure of

manhood in their society. They considered that they, and

they alone, were the “real” men at that time while all other

men were lesser mortals and of no value. To kill somebody

did not matter much according to the “Law of the Jungle”

they adopted. They were concerned only with themselves,

and considered that all other men had been put on this earth

to be destroyed or humiliated and humbled at their hands,

and according to their whim. It was quite clear that their

behaviour was no better than that of brutal wild animals,

and lacked any sense of humanity.

Such were the appalling principles of the criminals of the

towns before Officer Mohammad Emin Sheikho took up

the reins of security in many regions, for it was his wisdom,

genius and courage which would stamp out the injustice

perpetrated by these culprits and help them regain their

sense of rationality.

The story we are about to relate tells of one of these

transgressors: he was one of the strongest and most arrogant

of all the criminal leaders.

— صفحة 27 —

Stories of the Scholar

26

Nevertheless, he did not lack sound thinking, for having

seen that many of his like had repented to God at the hands

of our awe-inspiring officer, he decided to repent after he

thought of the line he had followed all his life, and the

horrible end that was awaiting him.

He thought and thought until he realised that death

would be his inevitable destination, as it would be for all

mankind, so how would he meet his Provider? He was aware

of his crimes and evil deeds; so what would his situation be

before God when He saw how he had hurt His servants,

killed some and stole from others? This sound logic led him

to take a positive decision, to change the course of his life

and to repent faithfully to God. He determined to turn his

back on all kinds of wickedness and shameful deeds, to

refrain from his disobedience to God and his practising

whatever is forbidden. He made up his mind to return to

God in repentance, just as many of his friends had done, and

follow the right path. There and then, he carried out his

decision and started a new stage of his life, marked by

straightness and obedience.

The amazing deeds of the bold officer, Mohammad Emin,

were the talk of the people of both quarters, al-Midan and al-

Shaghour. Even the comrades of this repentant criminal often

told of the schemes and exemplary punishments the officer

employed for chasing and arresting them. Indeed he always

managed to curtail the progress of their criminality and curb

them with his fearlessness. And so, because of the heroic deeds

— صفحة 28 —

The Officer, a Repentant Criminal and a Chicken Coop

27

of our officer this repentant criminal had heard about him,

but since he had never met him or even seen him accidentally,

he set about imagining various pictures of the officer’s

appearance, ‘He’s a tall, strong, brawny man, endowed with a

huge, muscular body… and surely he has a thick, black

moustache with curled ends covering much of his face.’ This

was the vision he had of the great officer, for such features

were the marks of manhood and courage amongst this type of

man. It was grossly exaggerated, as he imagined him to be

much bigger and broader and taller than any one of his own

criminal acquaintances.

One day, it happened that the repentant man was sitting

on a chair at the door of a wheat store in al-Midan quarter,

chatting with the owner of the store, a wheat merchant, when

the conversation turned to the head of the local police station:

how he chastised all criminals and defeated them, to the

extent that they were afraid of him and took to their heels

whenever they saw him. The merchant mentioned many

incidents when the officer had pursued the criminals in the al-

Midan and al-Shaqur quarters.

This was the subject of their conversation when Officer

Sheikho, the man they were talking about, crossed the street

before them, his willowy stature clothed in his smart khaki

uniform. He advanced briskly, so fleet of foot that one might

say he appeared to be flying. The merchant saw him and

pointing in his direction, he said to the repentant criminal,

— صفحة 29 —

Stories of the Scholar

28

‘Look! That’s him, the head of the police station, Officer

Sheikho.’

With great curiosity, the repentant man turned to have a

look at the superman whom he had imagined to be huge and

powerful. But… how strange! He did not see the coarse-

featured man he expected to see according to his own,

colourful imagination, and to what he had heard about the

officer and his overwhelming success when chasing the

former leader’s criminal friends!

Very strange indeed!

The officer was not endowed with a gigantic body and

taut muscles nor did he have a thick moustache, long and

curled at the ends; he was not a strutting, mighty man who

had bared his brown, powerful arms and stomped around

causing the earth to shake beneath his feet! The former

criminal failed to find any semblance of the physical shape

he had imagined. Instead, he saw a young, handsome man,

like a shining moon encircled with glory, walking with

graceful, but vigorous steps! How far removed was the fact

from the fiction! ‘I’m so confused!’ he thought. ‘Could this

really be the man who overpowers culprits, causes them

sleepless nights and instills horror in their hearts? Is this the

officer that controlled them all and caused them so much

trouble, who shredded their hopes with his iron fist and

formidable character?’

With that, the tradition of his criminal ignorance, the

seeds of which were still implanted within him, crept once

— صفحة 30 —

The Officer, a Repentant Criminal and a Chicken Coop

29

again into his mind to reveal itself through his words and

actions. So, being clearly annoyed because of the unexpected

sight he had just seen, he said in a loud voice, ‘Is this the

man whose very name has instilled terror in the hearts of

tough men? Shame on you, men of al-Midan! Shame on

you, ha… ha… powerful men! Is this person whose

appearance is as soft as that of a woman, the officer who

caused you so much trouble that you’re afraid even to

whisper his name? Again I say shame on all of you!’

But Godly Will refused to allow this repentant criminal

to continue with this wrongful judgement, so It gave him

the experience of a practical lesson to help him regain his

sense of reason and make him understand that courage

should not be judged according to physical shape and size,

but is born in the hearts of men who have an unwavering

belief in God that leads them to love justice and assist it.

And on the other hand, God holds victory in His Hands

and He grants it to those who follow His Straight Path and

seek truthfully to establish what is right and true.

So, in the evening of the day when the repentant

criminal had met our officer for the first time, he also met a

criminal from his old gang, who went by the name of Abu

al-Lail. He greeted him, ‘Hello,’ said Abu al-Lail, ‘How are

you, man? Welcome… welcome… master of all strong

men! Where have you been, man? We haven’t seen you for

a long time. We’ve really missed you, all the men have been

asking about you. They’re longing to see your handsome

chapters.title: صفحة 31 - 40 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 31 —

Stories of the Scholar

30

face. Don’t you miss your friends and hanker after the good

old days? Don’t you remember how great they were? By

God, we miss you so much.’ The repentant criminal replied

to his friend, ‘Oh Abu al-Lail! I’ve left behind my old

wrongful path and don’t have any more inclination for it.

For how much longer shall I continue to disobey my Lord

and hurt all those around me? No… I’ve had enough… it

was no way to live, I want to enjoy a safe and peaceful life.’

‘As you like my friend, it’s your own life and you’re free

to choose the path you want to follow. But don’t forget us,

my friend; let’s see you from time to time. And today I’m

inviting you to come to an evening entertainment with our

friends, just for them to see you and have a chat… you

don’t have to drink if you don’t want to; but it will make

us happy just to have your company.’

‘But…’ the repentant man replied, ‘how can I sit with

you while you drink wine, and break God’s Orders?’

‘What’s wrong in that my friend? We’ll be the ones

drinking, not you. You only have to sit with us so we can

enjoy each other’s company. We just want to see you because

the men have really missed you.’

And so, his friend insisted on the invitation and made

him promise to share their merry-making that night. And

so it was that with these friendly words, the repentant

criminal weakened and surrendered to his friend; he agreed

to join the men but only on condition that he would not

practise any forbidden acts with them.

— صفحة 32 —

The Officer, a Repentant Criminal and a Chicken Coop

31

Later that day, after the evening prayer, the two friends

met and headed towards the place where they would all

meet up to spend their night according to their whims and

fancies.

They went into an Arabian-style house with a large

courtyard surrounded by many rooms, with a fountain in

the centre. The owner of the house had given it over to illicit

purposes. Those who frequented the establishment wanted

to enjoy drinking wine, and amuse themselves just as they

liked. And for obvious reasons they had to hide within its

enclosing walls so as to be out of sight of the police, as such

gatherings were unlawful during the time of Ottoman rule.

In this way, this kind of people could enjoy their boisterous

entertainment without being held accountable.

When the two friends entered the brothel there was a

crowd of their fellow criminals inside, and so, having been

surprised at the arrival of their old friend, they rushed

towards the newcomer to give him a hearty welcome. They

embraced him one after another and showered him with

friendly words and happy smiles that soon made him forget

his repentance. He lost no time in rejoining their group

and becoming one of them once again, laughing along with

them, enjoying the raucous banter that appealed to them,

and enjoying the same things they took pleasure in.

The alcohol had not yet been offered to them, for some

were still arranging the bottles and cups on tables in a

special room, together with mixed nuts and other tidbits, so

— صفحة 33 —

Stories of the Scholar

32

that when the songstress began to sing songs to inspire

fornication and inflame forbidden desires their pleasure and

enjoyment would be complete.

The conversation went back and forth and moved from

one senseless topic to yet another even more degraded and

insignificant, and from time to time, noisy bursts of raucous

laughter rang out throughout the house: the barbarous,

irresponsible scene had clearly divorced itself from all sense

of humanity. They laughed and sang and then broke out in

spontaneous yells and shouts as if they had lost their minds.

They were entirely immersed in their debauchery… To

complete their enjoyment they were waiting only to clink

their wineglasses and drink a toast to each other and to

delight their ears with the music and songs of a harlot that

would inflame their desires.

This was the atmosphere inside that house when suddenly

someone let out a loud cry… in a voice that seemed to

tremble with fear, as it broke through that inhuman festival.

Instantly, absolute silence descended over the whole house

and all heads turned towards the source of the sound to find

out what was wrong. The person who had cried out had

come out of the room where the drinks and tidbits were

being prepared when he saw that the security forces had

climbed the walls of the house and were settled down in the

courtyard. There and then, a thunderous, dreadful voice

resounded throughout the whole house, making hearts

tremble and implanting a strange horror in the spirits of all

who were there, which caused them to lose their heads.

— صفحة 34 —

The Officer, a Repentant Criminal and a Chicken Coop

33

It was him, Aslan,

1 the awe-inspiring officer who had

arrived like a bolt from the blue with a squad of policemen.

And wasting no time they attacked the place like a cyclone

or a destructive thunderbolt.

What a peerless terrifying appearance this officer had!

What singular courage! What incomparable resolve he

displayed that never acknowledged the possibility of failure!

His voice tore down the mountains of disbelief and

infringements of God’s Orders settled in the hearts of those

criminals and thereby paralysed their powers and their

daring to practise wrongdoing and fornication. They all

heard the booming cry, which shook the walls of the house,

and they recognised its owner: it was him, the head of the

police station, in person. He was actually inside the house.

As soon as they realised this, their hearts leapt into their

mouths and all the strength fled from their bodies. They

had certainly not expected to face such a compromising

situation, for they had taken every precaution to be out of

sight so that no one might know anything about their

clandestine gathering. But unfortunately, their secret was

out and they would certainly receive a severe punishment.

The bold officer kept on railing at their cowardly evil

conduct, filling their hearts with trembling fear, and utterly

disrupting their gathering. Some of them cowered in front

of him while others tried to run away and rushed off like

startled wild asses, each one trying desperately to save

1 This was a nickname for Officer Sheikho and is translated as ‘Lion’.

— صفحة 35 —

Stories of the Scholar

34

himself. Still the brave officer, along with his men, leapt

towards them and many were arrested while just a few

managed to escape.

Now let us focus our attention on the repentant criminal,

the subject of our story, who had turned away from

repentance and turned instead back to the pleasures he had

enjoyed formerly with his old friends. When he heard the

thunderous voice of our officer rumbling throughout the

house he felt as though it had pervaded every molecule of his

body and he was struck by such overwhelming terror that his

limbs began to quiver. He could not control his tremors nor

could he understand what had come over him. A strange

feeling of terrifying and awesome fear had seemed to shackle

his limbs causing them to lose their strength until they felt

completely crushed. Truly, at that moment he felt that he

could not put up the least physical resistance, not even to a

little child. He had never previously, in all his life,

experienced such a terrible situation, ‘Where have my

manliness and strength disappeared to? I don’t understand

what’s happening to me!’ he said to himself. His rough

appearance was of no use to him for he had become like a

panic-stricken rabbit.

But what about his impressive, long, twirled moustache?

What about his bulging muscles and powerful body?

They were of no use to him either!

With great difficulty, and deathly pale, he gathered his

strength and went upstairs to the roof where he looked

— صفحة 36 —

The Officer, a Repentant Criminal and a Chicken Coop

35

around to find a safe hiding place… somewhere he could

avoid hearing the booming threats and menaces of the

courageous officer, the commandant of this patrol. But

there was no place for him to take shelter except in a

chicken coop situated at a corner of the roof; having no

other option he sneaked inside, crouched down and hoped

to be rescued from the lion’s ferocious attack.

Many hours passed while the brawny man hid in the

coop, his body trembling from head to toe, his heart

beating rapidly as his chest clearly moved up and down in

rhythm with its beating. Although the dauntless officer and

his men had left the house, having driven with them a

group of the criminals in shackles ready to be thrown into

prison, the criminal in question remained inside the coop

for many more hours even though he realised that the

danger had passed and he could come out safely. His teeth

were chattering as if he was in the midst of a bitterly cold

snow storm. He could not get over the extreme, strange

terror that struck him forcibly the moment he heard that

impressive, formidable voice of our officer. Finally, the

criminal decided to move out of his hiding place, and as he

did so his movements still displayed signs of the fear that

had overcome him.

He ran towards his home and entered while signs of

dumbfounding shock were still evident on his face and, in

fact, throughout his entire body. He threw himself on the

bed, but since he was terrified he could not possibly sleep.

— صفحة 37 —

Stories of the Scholar

36

He could not forget the events he had recently experienced

and was still wondering about the secret behind that voice

which caused the earth to shake under his feet. He had

spent a long life in crime and wrongdoing, how many times

had he been in difficult situations and faced being killed,

but, throughout it all he had never felt even the smallest

degree of the fear he felt when hearing the thunderous

shouts of Officer Sheikho.

He realised that this officer’s character was not to be

sniffed at and surely he was a man to be reckoned with! So

his criminal fellows had every right to have a thousand

apprehensions about this officer and to talk about him with

fear and trepidation. No doubt, the Almighty had dressed

him with an awe-inspiring appearance that caused them

many sleepless nights and made them think a many, many

times before daring to do any wrong.

The following morning, when the people who were

employed had gone to their place of work and started their

jobs, the repentant criminal set off in a hurry, heading

towards the police station intending to meet our brave

officer. He decided to apologise to him for mocking him

the day before, when he was in the wheat store, and to tell

him what had happened to him that same evening.

He entered Officer Emin Sheikho’s office at the police

station, and looked at our man with eyes full of reverence

and admiration. He greeted the officer, who replied with

his customary smile and kindness. Our officer invited the

— صفحة 38 —

The Officer, a Repentant Criminal and a Chicken Coop

37

repentant man to have a seat then called for his janitor to

bring a cup of coffee for the visitor.

‘How can I help you, brother?’ the venerable officer

asked his guest.

The repentant criminal replied, ‘Sir, I have something to

tell you.’

‘Yes, go ahead… tell me whatever you want.’

The repentant man began to speak and related his story

to the officer from the beginning up to the event that he

had experienced the day before his visit:

‘Oh sir, I was a criminal and it never troubled me to

commit any crime, either great or small, but thanks be to

God for I have returned to Him in repentance and regained

my sense of reason. But, sir, yesterday I said bad things

against you, and to speak frankly, sir, I even spat on the earth

damning the men of al-Midan quarter… how they claim to

be courageous and fear a man like you; I beg your pardon,

sir, for my stupid judgement about your appearance. When I

said this sir, you did not see me, for at that moment you

walked past without noticing me. But, sir, one of my old

friends, a former brother in crime, had invited me to join in

their revelry with them that evening and insisted on taking

me with him to their secret party. He said that he wanted me

to go because the men would be happy to see me for they

had missed me so much, and I was no longer obliged to

drink with them or share them with in practising what is

forbidden. That’s how he convinced me to go there with

— صفحة 39 —

Stories of the Scholar

38

him. But, sir, we had hardly finished saying hello and

reminiscing over the times we used to spend together when

suddenly you, accompanied by your men, broke into the

house we were in. Then, sir, I heard your terrible voice

thundering throughout the house. Truly, sir, I was overcome

by a feeling of such terror the like of which I had never

known before in my entire life. I would never forget the

awful moments I experienced when I heard your voice which

then threw me into a complete daze!

‘I climbed the stairs to the roof but don’t know how I

managed to do it for I felt petrified with fear, and there I

hid myself in a chicken coop so as to be out of your reach

and sight. Yes, sir, I confess that I was so afraid of you that

I even hid inside a dirty chicken coop!

‘By God, sir, even after you and your men left it was

many hours until I was able to control my fear and feel safe,

and still I found it difficult to come out of my hiding place

and head towards my home.

‘It was only then, sir, that I understood why evil men

repent and turn to God at your hands. And only then did I

excuse the strong men of al-Midan who fear you and avoid

meeting you. How could they not do that when your roaring

voice is like a cry of truth that paralyses wrongdoers, causes

their guilty hearts to shake and thus puts an end to their evil

ways! How could they not do that when your awe-inspiring

appearance at the moment of attack and confrontation razes

the mountains of criminality down to the ground.

— صفحة 40 —

The Officer, a Repentant Criminal and a Chicken Coop

39

So, I take back all that I said against you, sir, and I hope

that you may forgive me.’

When the repentant man finished his frank speech, our

officer opened the register lying on the table before him,

which included a list of the names of the criminals of the

town. He looked inside until he found the name of the

criminal before him, and then said to him ‘Yes… your

name is actually included on the list of repentant criminals.’

But there and then, the gentle tone of the officer’s voice

changed completely to one of firmness and censure just like

a rational, tender-hearted father, speaking to his son,

concerned about his future, while the repentant man stared

at him, dumbstruck and with his mouth gaping wide. Our

officer continued with his words of admonishment, saying,

‘Why did you agree to see them again and to spend the

evening with them after you had decided to repent and

turn to God? Is this acceptable? How did you agree to go

with him even if he insisted and swore at you to do so?

Why did you give in to him and comply with his mean and

dirty request? Don’t you know that when meeting with

these men it is natural for you to yearn for your past and

turn your back on repentance causing you to lose your life

here and in the other abode? Beware of doing such a thing

even one more time; you should give praise to God that He

saved you from their wily ways and that the matter ended

peacefully. You should promise your Lord that you will

never do this again.’

chapters.title: صفحة 41 - 50 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 41 —

Stories of the Scholar

40

The man was so affected by the noble officer’s

compassionate words of admonition that tears of sorrow

and relief coursed down his cheeks, for he fully regretted

what he had done. And so, he finally left the police station,

but not before he promised his Lord that he would not

associate with evil companions any more after the terrible

situation he had recently experienced and after the

conversation he had just had with the merciful officer. He

thanked his Provider for His Care for him and was

extremely grateful for the advice of the fearless, wise and

humane officer Mohammad Emin Sheikho.

The lesson we learn from this story is that true faith is

obtained when one is truly repentant, and this can be

accomplished by keeping away from forbidden actions and

from those who practise them. For even though a man may

refrain from committing wrongful deeds, if he keeps

company with evil people he will certainly return to his old

ways.

For it was said, “Tell me who your companions are and I

will tell you who you are.”

— صفحة 42 —

41

Danger Overcome on

the Al-Qaboon Highway

he Ottoman Empire lost its former strength and

glory and became like a sick old man compared with

the European States. This period of weakness began

towards the end of Turkish rule in the Arab countries where

criminality and depravity prevailed and disorder spread over

all areas. This came about as a result of the Ottoman Empire

giving up following the Orders of Almighty Al’lah.

For a certain time during that period, Officer Mohammad

Emin held the post of regional manager in Barzeh, which was

far from Damascus.

That entire area was covered by forest, and all the trees

which grew closely together for many kilometres, were tall and

abundant, rather like those in a tropical forest which made the

region a safe haven for criminals and some highway robbers

who lived there.

It was Friday when Officer Mohammad Emin left the

regional management office heading for his house in

Damascus where he had decided to spend his weekend and

T

— صفحة 43 —

Stories of the Scholar

42

seize the opportunity to deal with some personal matters.

But no sooner had he arrived at his house, than something

quite unexpected happened to him! He was afflicted with a

severe fever that made him stay in his bed, unable to leave it

without great difficulty. His temperature was very high

(about 40o C), causing him to sweat profusely. He was also

overcome by an extreme headache, backache and a sore

throat.

While lying in his bed in such a painful state, various

worrying thoughts came to his mind, ‘If I don’t go to work,

they will certainly say that I’m a coward and afraid to face

up to the current serious security situation. They will think

that l came away from the section and left the gendarme to

face a dangerous situation while I slackened off to enjoy the

safety and security of my home.… I’m sure that’s what they

will say about me… but, oh my God! This terrible fever has

overcome me and forced me to keep to my bed… so how

can I possibly go to work?’

It was an extremely difficult position for any brave man

to be faced with, and especially for our noble officer, for he

truly preferred death to being accused of cowardice and

facing defeat… he would have preferred that the ground

might open up and swallow him rather than be accused

falsely of cowardice and weakness. Then he continued

discussing his critical position, ‘No… no… I don’t want

any false stories to be circulated about me… I shall get up

now and go to my work.’

— صفحة 44 —

Danger Overcome on the Al-Qaboon Highway

43

The serious breaches of security on the road to Barzeh –

especially during those troubled times – would certainly

expose travellers to attacks by criminals or other hooligans

who would seize the opportunity during the time of political

confusion and lack of security to carry out violent attacks and

robberies. So, despite his illness, Officer Sheikho decided to

go to the section at whatever cost to himself, for refused to let

any of the leaders mention the word “coward” in regard to

him for he was the so-called Aslan

1… and known for his

unparalleled bravery .

After taking this decision, he called out to his mother in

his weak and weary voice, ‘Oh mother! Would you bring

me my military uniform!’

She replied in a voice full of sympathy and compassion,

‘What! What do you say my dear son… your military

uniform? But you’re in such a bad state! You have a fever

and cannot get up… you are soaked by your own sweat…

Oh my son! May Al’lah be pleased with you… stay in your

bed until you recover, by Al’lah’s Will, then you can go if

you want to.’

But he begged her, ‘Please bring it mother… if you

won’t… I’ll do it myself… bring it to me and get yourself

ready to go with me… tell my wife too.’

His mother gave in for she realised just how determined

he was: she knew that when he decided to do something,

1 Aslan means ‘Lion’ in Arabic and was the nickname given to Officer Sheikho

because of his bravery

— صفحة 45 —

Stories of the Scholar

44

nothing could make him change his mind. So she brought

the uniform to him, and helped him to put it on, and when

he was ready, they went downstairs and out to the street

where a horse-drawn cab was waiting for him.

He could hardly walk, and had to lean heavily on his

mother and wife until he reached the cab. It was drawn by a

pair of horses and had a door at the back with an adjustable

hood that covered it and separated them from the driver who

sat in his seat in the front. When they had all got into the

cab, Aslan called out to the driver, ‘Let’s go to Barzeh…

driver.’

The driver was amazed and terrified, and thought to

himself, ‘Does anyone dare to go to Barzeh in these dangerous

times when no man can be sure of coming back alive?’ and he

said stuttering, ‘To… to Bar… to Barzeh sir? To Barzeh?’

Thereupon, Aslan shouted at him, ‘Let’s go!’

He turned as pale as a corpse and his lips moved without

uttering a single sound. He had no choice but to drive off

in the cab, all the while thinking that the end of his life

would come sooner rather than later!

The cab set off at top speed along the road which was

covered by a canopy of the tall leafy trees that shut out the

sunshine, while the suffering officer laid his head on his

mother’s knee and stretched out his legs towards his wife,

then he closed his eyes and could not even try to open them

because of the severe fever and pains which he was suffering.

The cab was dashing along, its wheels bouncing noisily

over the stones with the cab swaying from side to side while

— صفحة 46 —

Danger Overcome on the Al-Qaboon Highway

45

the patient was groaning softly due to his great pain… a

most unusual situation, however ill he felt.

As for his poor mother, she bent over him, her eyes full

of mercy and sympathy, feeling his suffering and sharing

his pain.

The journey continued in this way until they reached

Tora Bridge, the little bridge, about six metres long, that

crossed the Yazid River, a branch of the Barada. And right

there is where something serious happened.

While Officer Mohammad Emin was still suffering from

the severe fever, lying in the same position, he felt drops of

water falling on his hot, flushed face. He opened his eyes

and saw his mother’s tears running down her face. He felt

that the cab was stopping, so he asked, ‘What’s the matter,

Mother? Why are you crying?’

She was barely able to speak, and with a deep sigh she

said, ‘We’ll certainly be disgraced… we’ll all be killed…

they are highwaymen.’

No sooner had she finished speaking than he leaped up

like a lion ready to face grave danger! With a single kick, he

broke the door off the cab and followed this by leaping out

to face one of the highway robbers pointing his gun toward

the cab. Without a moment’s hesitation, he punched the

criminal’s face with all his might. With this unexpected

ferocious attack, the robber felt as if a thunder bolt had

smashed into his head and he fell to the ground, unconscious,

with his pistol beside him.

— صفحة 47 —

Stories of the Scholar

46

The brave officer then turned to the front of the cab and

found the second robber had fled with his pistol after he

had seen what had happened to his crony.

The robber could never have expected this outcome!

How had it happened?… and all within just a few seconds!

He was terrified so he ran off wanting nothing more than

saving himself after shooting at the driver who, trembling

with fear, raised his hands up to surrender.

But that brave officer did not let the criminal go, and he

ran after him at amazing speed until he grabbed him. He

beat him and took the gun from him, then he dragged him

to the cab where his crony was lying on the ground

unconscious. He tied them together to the back of the cab,

and then went back to lying down with his head on his

mother’s knee and his legs stretched out towards his wife;

whereupon he began groaning again because of the severe

pain he was still suffering , with glistening drops of sweat

dripping from his noble forehead.

The danger that had surrounded them suddenly

disappeared, and the feeling that they were surely about to

die left his mother and wife along with it.

When the two highway robbers had stopped the cab,

and one of them had fired his gun at the driver, and the

other one at the travellers, the wife thought that they would

surely be killed as she knew that her poor husband was

unable to do so much as stand up. She had never expected

or even imagined that her husband might do such a deed or

show such great ability.

— صفحة 48 —

Danger Overcome on the Al-Qaboon Highway

47

‘How could he instantly overcome illness and weakness

and rush with such strength that I had never seen the like

of before! He looked like a powerful, leaping lion and was

able to arrest two armed men while he was unarmed and

had a high fever! How was he able to do that? And what

bravery had possessed this man! What high aspiration and

wonderful willpower had burst in his spirit to make the

impossible possible, turn weakness into strength, and with a

single outburst, defend the truth. What determination he

had shown before which all difficulties break down and

duplicity is destroyed and wiped out!’

That was what Mohammad Emin’s wife thought to

herself.

That wonderful sight made her prostrate herself before

her husband, showing her true appreciation as she had never

seen him react like that before. She had heard a lot about his

fearless, manly deeds, his courage, and his capabilities, but

now she witnessed him in action… she witnessed the reality

of his deeds.

When they arrived at the police station, he put the two

arrested men in a cell until the following day, by which

time when he was feeling somewhat better. He sent for the

robbers to investigate their case, and he found that it was

only dire need that had forced them to follow such a bad,

criminal road; for each of them had a family and could

barely provide food to keep his children alive since he had

no job to earn his livelihood legally.

— صفحة 49 —

Stories of the Scholar

48

At that time, with the demise of the Ottoman Empire,

disorder and anarchy controlled the country and unemployment

was rife; many jobs in all fields were lost, and men were unable

to provide even basic necessities for their families.

Because of the difficult circumstances these men had

suffered, which forced them to do such wrong inhumane

deeds, Officer Mohammad Emin forgave them and released

them after giving them sufficient money to support their

families for many months.

Thus, his conduct always displayed his great mercy and

compassion. Before punishing the robber or wrongdoer you

must investigate his situation. If he steals due to force of

necessaity, help him. But if he robs again though he is no

longer in need, this act shall be seen as arising from a spiritual

defect and then you have the right, no, the obligation to arrest

and punish him in order to uproot the affliction and evil from

his spirit.

Many days later, after he heard of Aslan’s illness and

spectacular deed on the dangerous road to Barzeh, the

commander visited him. He had also heard of the strange,

remarkable story of the arrest of the highway robbers, and

totally astonished he addressed the officer, ‘Aslan! How did

you dare to take such a risk under such serious circumstances?

You know… if I were you I would never have gone!’

‘Oh sir… Commander! I want you to swear by God that

if I had not gone, that you would not say that I was a

coward.’ Aslan replied.

— صفحة 50 —

Danger Overcome on the Al-Qaboon Highway

49

‘Yes… by God I would,’ the Commander said.

Then he remained silent preoccupied with thoughts of

the officer’s amazing courage and willpower, and respect for

this exalted, honourable spirit.

What a great risk! And truly all people should be like

him and place their trust in God.

chapters.title: صفحة 51 - 60 (Obsequious Behaviour Is not Tolerated)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 51 —

50

Obsequious Behaviour Is not Tolerated

ear reader, the story we are about to relate may be

a practical interpretation of the reality of the

noble verse, “Honour belongs to Al’lah and His

Envoys, and to the believers.”

1

You might also find other relevant points and glean

useful lessons from it.

The events of this story took place in Barzeh, in the

region of Ghutah, the verdant and fertile oasis of Damascus,

at the time when our noble man, Mohammad Emin

Sheikho, held the post of regional manager there.

This region was notable for its wide open spaces and vast

areas of arable land. Some of it was forested, while other

parts were planted with various kinds of grain, greenery and

vegetables. The region was in a sorry state before our

magnanimous officer took up his post there. Due to the

condition of the area, a feudatory held power over the

people; he greatly exploited them but they were powerless

to do anything about their situation. He deprived them of

the fruits of their labour and the wages for their work,

1 The Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 63, e Hypocrites (al-Munafiqun), verse 8.

D

— صفحة 52 —

Obsequious Behaviour Is not Tolerated

51

which meant that the farmer and his family might go to

bed hungry after a long day spent labouring in the fields.

The feudatory of whom we write had amassed great

wealth by bribing previous managers and their gendarmes to

encourage them to shut their eyes to his depriving the people

of their rights and seizing their land. This enabled him to go

to extremes in his oppression: he broke all laws, with nothing

and no one to deter him, and no man to stand up to his

tyranny. But, would he persist in this oppression? And

would matters continue in the same way as that overlord

expected once our honest officer Aslan took up his post? For

this unscrupulous man had dealt with many regional

managers before our officer arrived, and his business was

always facilitated by them because of the large bribes with

which he bought their passive compliance and encouraged

them to close their eyes to his wrongdoing.

Therefore, when Officer Mohammad Emin took up his

post, the overlord attached no importance to the matter, and

as he had always done with past regional managers, he

immediately went to see him, to sweet-talk him and grovel

before him, offering his services and assistance, and showing

his false admiration for the new officer in order to earn his

favour; just as he had done with previous managers.

The meeting proceeded in the usual manner and Officer

Mohammad Emin spoke to the feudatory and thanked him

for his sentiments and kind offer, but he was fully aware of

what lay behind that obsequiousness. It was for the personal

— صفحة 53 —

Stories of the Scholar

52

benefits he sought to achieve by denying the rights of others

and asking our officer to ignore the unlawful acts that he had

no intention of giving up.

But, dear reader, would he achieve his evil aims?

Certainly, the overlord believed that nothing would change

as he was confident that with large sums of money, he could

buy the officer’s acquiescence in his ruthless aims.

When Officer Mohammad Emin set out to introduce

reform and bring about change throughout the entire

agricultural area of that region, he faced many difficulties

but, as always, he overcame them. And after only a few days

of the officer’s reformative actions the feudatory was shocked

by an incident he certainly had not expected! For the new

manager stood in the way of his exploitation and oppression

of the local people. He realised immediately the gravity of his

position, so he rushed off to see the new manager to grovel

once again and flatter him with his soft words, offering his

services and assistance in any way possible. And he did not

stop there, for he realised that this approach had not been

successful the first time, so he brought with him some

precious gifts, even though he was known to be an extremely

stingy man. But in fact, he found a reaction which he did

not expect, for the regional manager adamantly, but politely,

refused all the presents and gifts.

The disappointed feudatory left the section office, but day

after day he tried to approach the honest officer cringing

before him and asking him to overlook his unlawful actions.

— صفحة 54 —

Obsequious Behaviour Is not Tolerated

53

In fact, the truth that was settled within the spirit of this

upright, honest officer made the feudatory’s aims impossible

to achieve. His evil actions were no longer possible because of

the existence of the honest master, Mohammad Emin, who

dispelled oppression and reinstated the rights of the people.

As for the overlord, he did not stop in his efforts to get

close to the officer and continued to show his great love and

admiration; many times he sought to bring the officer to his

house for a banquet, but he never succeeded.

Thus, he got no support for his wrongdoing from that

noble master, and so he came to hate him, but he was as sly

as a fox, for he cleverly hid his hatred and showed nothing

but love and obsequious tactics, trying to earn the officer’s

satisfaction and compliance.

That was how the matter progressed until this honest

officer moved to another section, and the day of his departure

would never be forgotten by the feudatory. For him it was a

day of great happiness, for the man who had stood firmly in

the way of his oppression and tyranny had left, so he could

return to his unlawful acts as there was no longer anyone to

call him to account.

One day, while that upright man, Mohammad Emin,

was sitting in his house, there was a knock at the door. He

opened it to find one of his acquaintances there, a person

he did not know very well. The visitor greeted Mohammad

Emin who welcomed him amicably and received him in a

hospitable way.

— صفحة 55 —

Stories of the Scholar

54

Inside the house, the guest soon stated the reason for his

visit. ‘Abu Fathi… you selfless man! I want you to help me

through your knowledge… I want to buy some arable land

in the region of al-Ghoutah where you used to work. I’m

sure you had many acquaintances there, and you can help

me to achieve my aim through them. Would you do me a

favour and help me with this?’

Mohammad Emin replied, ‘Yes, certainly… by Al’lah’s

Will I’ll do my best to help with what you want.’

The guest smiled, and his increasing optimism was

displayed on his face, as he said, ‘This is exactly what I

expected from you… you have never changed… rather you

grow more kind and generous, and your essence becomes

even purer and more brilliant. Thank you very much…

may Al’lah reward your goodness.’

Half an hour passed in pleasant and agreeable conversation,

then the guest left in cheerful high spirits after the two men had

made an appointment to discuss the results of Mohammad

Emin’s enquiries.

Our righteous man recalled the days that he had served in

that section, then he remembered that despicable overlord,

and his bootlicking and attempted bribery, so he decided to

visit him the next day.

In the morning, before setting off to the area which was

not far away, he sat for a while to think about the journey,

for it might need some planning, especially as he had heard a

lot about the feudatory’s extreme miserliness, from people of

— صفحة 56 —

Obsequious Behaviour Is not Tolerated

55

the region. Therefore, our officer immediately decided to go

to the market and buy one kilo of fresh meat, then he

ordered it to be grilled and added some vegetables. He

folded it in a piece of flatbread and wrapped it; then he

headed off to the Barzeh section where he had once occupied

the post of regional manager.

Driven by the intention of carrying out the kind deed

which the acquaintance had asked him to do, his forthcoming

journey filled him with great pleasure.

Mounting his unique white horse, he passed through the

orchards of al-Ghoutah and its lush orange groves, enjoying

its cool soft breezes that carried the aromas of various fruits

and the sweet fragrance of roses and flowers. When he

reached the countryside he was in a state of great joy and

spiritual relief as he headed for the house of the feudatory.

When the local people saw him, they longed for his return

and for the time when fairness prevailed. No one he met in

the lanes of the countryside passed him without smiling and

raising a hand in greeting, saying, ‘Welcome sir… welcome…

come in please!’

As for Officer Aslan, he returned their greetings in the

best way, with a constant smile on his noble countenance,

and kind and gentle words for all of them.

When he arrived at the overlord’s house, still mounted

on his white horse, he approached the door, then stretched

out his leg and gave a powerful kick at the door!

After a few moments the door was opened to reveal the

overlord in person…and what a great surprise he received

— صفحة 57 —

Stories of the Scholar

56

for it was the former regional manager himself who had

banged at the door! It was not a pleasant surprise, in fact it

was such a shock that it brought a frown to his face and his

countenance darkened!

The venerable officer greeted him and the feudatory

returned his greeting; then Mohammad Emin asked him if

he had any arable land for sale, or knew someone who

wanted to sell a piece of land in the region.

The overlord held such hateful feelings towards our

officer that his face paled at the very sight of him; and

completely lacking in any kind of chivalry or respect he

replied in a very rough manner, ‘No… I don’t have any land

for sale, and I don’t know anyone who wants to sell land.’

And instantly he retreated and shut the door without

uttering another word, contrary to his past manner, when

his friendly honeyed phrases full of hypocrisy had flowed

from his tongue and he had greatly exaggerated in showing

false respect and high praise for Officer Sheikho. But now,

he did not invite the officer to enter the house… or even

utter a single word… he simply shut the door.

Mohammad Emin had never received such treatment

from him when he held his post as a regional manager of

the district, but he knew him well and understand all that

he had heard about the man’s miserliness, stinginess and

lack of chivalry, so he left and set off to look for a piece of

land of the requested specifications until he found it.

He then returned to the feudatory and kicked at the door

once again while still mounted on his horse. The miserable

— صفحة 58 —

Obsequious Behaviour Is not Tolerated

57

man opened the door and this time it was only his head that

appeared around the edge of the door as he asked, ‘What do

you want?’

Officer Aslan replied, ‘Hey you… listen to me… whoever

knocks at the door with his foot… does not stretch out his

hand to ask for help. Thank God that I have not dismounted

my horse, and my actions were correct when I did not allow

you to encroach upon anyone’s rights; nor did I eat any food

with which you tried to tempt me. Know that he who

stretches his leg, does not offer his hand.’

Then he took out the wrapped food and opened it to

display the grilled meat and he addressed the feudatory,

‘I’m sure you won’t offer me anything more delicious than

this meat… I don’t need you, nor do I need your welcome

or invitation to have food. I thank God that I have never

once been deceived by you.’

He turned his horse forcefully, showing great disdain for

the deeds and character of the overlord, and hurried off to a

pleasantly cool and shady place where there flowed a creek of

sparkling water. He sat there and spread open the package of

meat and ate happily and cheerfully. When he was sated, he

went to the bank of the creek and drank from its fresh cold

water, then he praised God most highly for His Graces and

for enabling him to distinguish between good and evil, for

he had expected the treatment that he received from the

feudatory and had never been deceived by him either now or

in the past. He knew well that his previous kind treatment

— صفحة 59 —

Stories of the Scholar

58

and his bootlicking and offering of presents, services, and

invitations to banquets – which were always met by our

officer’s refusal – were only to serve the overlord’s personal

interests and base purposes which he might attain through

the executive power of our honourable officer, Aslan. But

now that Mohammad Emin had moved to another region,

that shameful man had no further use for him, therefore he

was neither welcomed nor received hospitably as a guest.

The despicable man used to welcome only those guests

whom he thought could further his personal interests, but to

welcome and receive them for mere humane or friendly

purposes would be a loss in his sight.

Officer Mohammad Emin had left that region happily

thanking God that he had upset the obsequious overlord

but had not displeased Al’lah, for he had never complied

with that contemptible man in any of his wrongdoing or

oppression.

Such was the glorious course of Mohammad Emin

Sheikho, for by his words and deeds he aimed only to

satisfy Al’lah: Glory to His Splendour.

— صفحة 60 —

59

Superior Intelligence Resolves

a Difficult Situation

here came a time when the Ottomans changed and

lowered their moral standards: they abandoned

Al’lah’s Book (the Holy Qur’an) and replaced It with

temporal laws devised by man. So it pleased Al’lah to cause

them to be removed from the countries they had governed, as

their staying there was giving rise to actual and moral

destruction. After they withdrew from our country (al-Sham,

Greater Syria) and because of the collapse of the Ottoman

Empire, Mohammad Emin Sheikho no longer held his rank

as an officer in the security services. He had been a manager of

the castle and its prisons, and it was his responsibility to

maintain security and uphold the law against criminals and

corruption. And so he became an ordinary citizen like any

other, and no longer held any official rank, nor did he have

any other employment.

One day, while he was walking along a street in Damascus

on his way to buy some household requirements, he chanced

across one of the malevolent criminals he had come up against

as an officer. So, the criminal was quick to grab his chance to

T

chapters.title: صفحة 61 - 70 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 61 —

Stories of the Scholar

60

hurt the dignity of the man who had pursued him relentlessly,

punished him, and even put him in jail.

As soon as the criminal recognised him, his vicious tongue

knew no limits in expressing his delinquency and baseness. He

was yelling all manner of vile threats to that pure humane

man, Mohammad Emin, and muttering to himself, ‘Your

days are numbered! You’re nothing now… your time of glory

is over… you’re not an officer now!’

That hardened criminal would not care even if it came to

a fight as his enemy was no longer an officer, and was now

just an ordinary citizen with no particular power over him.

Mohammad Emin heard the words and knew exactly which

criminal it was, but he hurried to the market followed by the

foul-mouthed man till he disappeared into the crowd.

He could have attacked the criminal and thrown him to

the ground with just one punch as he had done once with

their boss “Hamu Jamu”, (the leader of the criminal gangs),

because not only did he excel in the arts of fighting, but he

possessed great courage and feared none but Al’lah.

But he realised that if he followed that course of action

he would end up in jail along with the criminal, degrading

himself by being sentenced to prison and being thrown in

with all sorts of felons, drug addicts, thieves and other such

people.

Therefore he thought, ‘I’ll bide my time… I won’t beat

or punish him now… every problem has a solution, and

this one, by Al’lah’s Will, will surely be solved.’

— صفحة 62 —

Superior Intelligence Resolves a Difficult Situation

61

Having completed his purchases Mohammad Emin

hurried back to his home, where he sat alone, in a pensive

state of mind, analysing the matter from all sides with the aim

of finding a solution. He thought, ‘I’ll be exposed repeatedly

to such situations as I was today… as there are a lot of

criminals who were caught and punished when I was an

officer… they will flourish now and try to take revenge, or

even kill me.’

He mulled over the matter, again and again, till he

reached a solution but he kept it to himself. With newfound

vigour, and the strength of a lion, he left the house again,

whereupon he happened to meet one of the truly hardened

criminals. He rushed up to him, smiling broadly and greeted

him as a long lost friend. The criminal was taken totally by

surprise and looked at him in utter astonishment. Then he

respectably saluted him wondering what on earth was going

on. ‘Hello, sir!’ he said, as he was still accustomed to greeting

this man politely and, too, because of the formidable

character of this august former officer which was imprinted

on his mind… the very same officer who had constantly

pursued and punished them.

His astonishment increased even further when Mr.

Mohammad Emin said to him, ‘Where have all you men

got to? I miss you… I’d be so happy to live near you. I’m

tired of living with all that “garbage” (as the criminals

referred to ordinary people, so he spoke to him in their own

“language”).’ He added, ‘I’ll be miserable unless I see you

— صفحة 63 —

Stories of the Scholar

62

men more often, and I’d be honoured if you and some of

your friends would come to eat with me tomorrow. I want

you to invite the real men, the toughest criminals… not

those who have only killed one or two people and claimed

that they’re real men… no, I want the heroes that have

killed at least five, and I want the bravest ones, like you.’

Initially taken aback, the gang leader was then overwhelmed

with delight at the invitation to eat with the former officer.

The criminal answered, ‘Yes, sir! At your command!’ for as he

heard the words ‘eat with me’ he knew that the food would be

excellent and their reception friendly and hospitable. Then he

continued, ‘Tomorrow sir, I’ll come to you with three or four

of the toughest men that I’m sure you will admire.’

Mohammad Emin, the sagacious man, replied, ‘What did you

say?… three or four men? No… no.’

The criminal asked him, ‘So, how many tough men shall

I bring, sir?’ Mohammad Emin replied, ‘Fifteen or more…

twenty. Tomorrow I want you to honour me with twenty

courageous men as dear esteemed guests, for I truly miss

being in the company of brave, daring men.’

The criminal dashed off, delighted to carry the good news

to many of the top criminals that they were invited for an

excellent meal with their honourable, faithful “friend”. And

so, it was that he gathered together twenty of the most

hardened criminals of the city.

At home, Mohammad Emin had ordered to be prepared

for them two whole sheep stuffed with rice and delicacies

cooked by expert chefs, as well as a variety of other tasty

— صفحة 64 —

Superior Intelligence Resolves a Difficult Situation

63

foods and excellent fruits and mixed nuts. He had all of the

food placed on a raised dais in the shady courtyard of his

house. He also brought them eight sets of playing cards and

then, finally, he placed his tall chair behind a little table in an

elevated spot close to a wall, and sat with his narghile,

1 which

had been specially prepared for the occasion. He remained

there, relaxed and at ease, to await the arrival of twenty of

the biggest criminals, who had accepted his invitation with

great pleasure. As soon as they knocked at the door, he

opened it and received them hospitably, saying, ‘Welcome to

you, brave men, my home is your home! I miss you so

much… and I hope you will all stay very much a part of my

life.’ These friendly words served to whet their appetite for

the delicious food to come, as there were so many good

things to look forward to: roasted, stuffed sheep… fruits…

and spending time in enjoyment and pleasure, and all of that

at no cost to them. They were more than happy when they

sat to eat and could hardly believe the extent of the banquet.

They feasted their eyes and ate their fill till they were fully

satiated, while Mohammad Emin remained seated on his

chair, smoking his narghile.

Once they had eaten their fill, some of them started to

wash up all the utensils and dishes, and put them back in

place in the kitchen, they also cleaned the kitchen and rinsed

the floor,

2 and then they returned to sit in the courtyard to

1 A water pipe used for smoking which originated in the Near East.

2 They were accustomed to doing this for themselves, so they did it for their

new “friend” too.

— صفحة 65 —

Stories of the Scholar

64

play cards, feeling happy and replete, to drink strong Arabic

coffee. They relaxed like this till the sun was beginning to

set, when the criminal who was the guest of honour said to

them that they should go and leave their master to relax.

So, they all stood up and took their leave of him. Then,

their kind host, Mohammad Emin, said to them, ‘Listen

men! I really enjoy being in your company, so I’m inviting

any of you who have nothing better to do to come and

spend the evening relaxing and having fun; I don’t like to

be alone and I want a few bold men to keep me company…

my life is boring without you men around.’

‘At your command, sir!’ they said, and left the house.

In this way, it became the habit for them to pass most

nights at Mohammad Emin’s home playing cards and

drinking coffee.

One day, Mohammad Emin went out on the road on a

matter of business, in the company of his entourage of fifteen

strong, tough men: some on his right and the others on his

left. He stood amongst them like the moon surrounded by its

halo, or the lion with its cubs. They all yielded to him and

were at his beck and call. Previously he had held his position

of authority as the officer in charge of many policemen and he

now held the reins of power through another, different group

of men; and so he established justice and security in the

country at a time when it was passing through harsh

conditions due to many political and security twists and turns.

This was the time shortly after the exit of Turkey from Syria

and it became occupied by the French.
