— صفحة 66 —

Superior Intelligence Resolves a Difficult Situation

65

This was a time when peace and stability faltered and

confusion reigned.

In fact, the residents of the neighbourhood began to regard

him as the master and commander of his escorts, the leading

criminals, and one day their neighbour expressed her

astonishment to his wife, saying, ‘Your husband has really

confused us! We knew him once as a religious man, highly

respected by sheikhs, but now we find him as the commander

of a band of criminals… so, is he a religious man or the leader

of a group of bold men?’

One day, as usual, Mohammad Emin was out with his

entourage of criminals, and came across the criminal who

had insulted him on the street. Mohammad Emin pounced

upon him as quick as lightning, leaving his men behind.

Lightly and swiftly, he cuffed the criminal twice saying,

‘Why did you abuse me?’

Hastily the criminal pulled back and loaded his gun

directing it towards our quick-witted man but, what a

surprise! Within a few moments Mohammad Emin saw him

being hurled up above the heads of his entourage and then

thrown to the ground, where they assaulted and disarmed

him. Showing no mercy, they hauled him off the ground and

dragged him to the bank of the Yazid river, (a tributary of the

Barada), pulling out their knives to kill him and cast him in

the river, as if killing a man was a normal, everyday matter.

Suddenly aware of their intentions Mohammad Emin

cried out, ‘No… no… men! I don’t want you to stain your

— صفحة 67 —

Stories of the Scholar

66

knives with his tainted blood… leave him, it isn’t worth

dirtying your knives on his filthy body!’

Our man was not only courageous, but also intelligent

and quick-thinking. He did not want them to kill the

criminal, for he believed killing should be avoided whenever

possible, so he spoke to them using the words and kind of

language they were accustomed to hearing.

As soon as the order was given they let him go and

pulled him to his feet, but every last one of them was quite

bemused at the order not to kill him… while the reprieved

culprit stood trembling like a straw in a strong wind,

unable to believe that he was still alive.

Then, Mohammad Emin continued, ‘I want all of you

men to spread the word of what has happened here today.

Tell all bold men that this man’s blood has been shed in

vain and let those of you who are here tell all those who are

not. So, anyone who sees him anywhere in this country,

after this day, should kill him immediately as this will be

considered a lawful action.’

The culprit could not believe his luck! He was still alive

even though a band of hardened criminals led by a former

police officer had been about to kill him. But he did not

stop to question why.

Then, not wanting to tempt fate he deserted the state of

Syria and never came back.

— صفحة 68 —

67

The False Penitent Will Never Succeed

certain hardened criminal repented, turned his back

on his former life of crime and started to attend the

mosque in a particular area of Damascus. He took

his place behind the imam every day at all the appointed

times of prayer for forty consecutive days. He got up for the

dawn-prayer and would even enter the mosque before the

imam himself.

The imam was astonished at the radical change that had

come over the man and his sincere repentance, for it is well-

known among the sheikhs that: ‘If man perseveres in praying

at collective prayers (at the mosque) for forty days, he is then

considered to be one of the believers’ and… ‘if you see the

man frequent the mosque, then testify to his belief.’

What great contrition he showed! That desperate bandit

repented from his life of crime… he stopped killing and

robbing, and despoiling all in his path in order to turn to a

life of rectitude and prayer. No-one, not even the most

righteous of young men could have displayed greater

sincerity than he did. This youth seemed to have turned to

a path of true repentance and great integrity so that he

A

— صفحة 69 —

Stories of the Scholar

68

compared most favourably with the best of other youths in

the neighbourhood.

The sheikh (imam) had noticed all of his newfound

qualities of character, so he expressed his great admiration

and encouragement, telling him how pleased he was with

him for this remorse and subsequent attendance at all

prayer services every day.

What is more important is that no sooner had the forty

days passed than the repentant youth went to the house of

his sheikh where he received an especially warm welcome as

the sheikh was so heartened that this was a man who had

foresworn his former life of crime and wrongdoing, and

now turned to the sheikh for guidance.

On entering the house he wasted no time at all and

immediately made a proposal of marriage to the sheikh’s

daughter: not only had he rejected his life of crime and

turned to devout prayer, he also wanted to be a son-in-law

of the sheikh!

The sheikh was so pleased with his request and accepted

the proposal without any delay, wanting to consolidate the

relationship between them so that he would be encouraged

to continue on his path of repentance and not be tempted

to return to his former life of crime.

Surely by this alliance, he would not stray from his path

of repentance and would continue to worship Al’lah, his

Provider for his wife-to-be was the daughter of the sheikh,

and so his father-in-law was the imam himself.

— صفحة 70 —

The False Penitent Will Never Succeed

69

But…! This youth, who appeared to have turned away

from his life of crime and shown true repentance was actually

planning a despicable deed! As the proverb says, “I kept

praying until I got my request, and when I got it, I stopped

praying.”

The sheikh’s daughter was a captivating beauty, and the

description of her allure had been circulated on the tongues of

some ignorant women in the neighbourhood until it reached

the ears of this sly fox; devilish thoughts came to his mind

and, slowly but surely, he began to formulate his malicious

intention… and so he resorted to his dishonest show of

“repentance” in order to achieve his purpose.

And it was not long until he showed his true colours!

Once the sheikh’s daughter became his wife and went to live

in his home, he took off his mask of righteousness. His real

intention behind the façade of repentance was unveiled…

and within a few days of the marriage he brought home a

group of criminals who were every bit as odious as him.

Bottles of wine were brought out and his evil purpose was

revealed: he wanted to trade in his wife’s honour and earn

money from her. He wanted to use his wife as a prostitute!

This was shocking to any right minded person!

He went in to her room and told her about the men

who were coming, which she found quite strange. Then

when he added that he wanted her to entertain them she

thought she was going crazy…

chapters.title: صفحة 71 - 80 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 71 —

Stories of the Scholar

70

What? Surely she must have misunderstood him! Is that

really what he wanted from her? She could not believe what

she heard!

How dreadful! She was a pure, chaste woman who had

been brought up and educated in the ways of purity and

uprightness at the hands of a virtuous upright man.

It was a severe shock, but fortunately she was clever

enough not to react; she knew that if her husband got any

idea that she was appalled at his suggestion he would

quickly set out to destroy her.

She told him to wait a moment, pretending that she

wanted to use the bathroom and he told her to be quick as

his friends were waiting for her. As soon as he had joined

them she ran to her room… grabbed a cloak to cover herself

and fled from the house, barely able to see her way because

of her fear and the terrible shock she had just received. And

thank God that she had the presence of mind to act so

quickly! She arrived at her family’s house and could hardly

believe that she had managed to escape from that beast and

his evil intentions. Her father was most surprised to see her

in such a distressed state as she tried to relate the details of

the incident to him despite her floods of tears.

He was soon in a state of shock! How could he have

been taken in by this man?

He was frustrated because his usual impeccable judgement

had been proved to be completely flawed. The imam had

thought the young man to be truly repentant, a man who had

— صفحة 72 —

The False Penitent Will Never Succeed

71

turned to worshiping his Provider, and so he had lost no time

in giving that poor girl, his daughter, in marriage to him so

that he might continue on his path towards true closeness to

his Provider. But he was shocked to find him a sly and

malevolent man.

As he became aware of the full truth of the matter he

grew even more aggrieved and said to his daughter in a sad

voice, with his eyes brimming with tears, ‘Forgive me my

daughter… forgive me… may Al’lah punish him… may

Al’lah take revenge for us.’

As for the criminal, there was no one to hold him back.

He wondered why she was taking so long to come back to

the room and he called her but there was no answer. Then

the truth dawned… she had outwitted him and run back to

her family!

He was furious but thought that she could not escape

from his grasp, so he went to his father-in-law’s house and

began to pound at the door. They knew it was him and

were afraid as there was no man in the house to defend

them except her father, the poor aged sheikh.

They did not open the door… and they even locked the

door of the room for extra security, then the criminal –

who would stop at nothing – raised his voice so that all the

neighbours heard his shouts, ‘I want my wife… I want my

wife back… I’m telling you… send my wife back to me

otherwise you’ll be sorry.’ He repeated this appalling

behaviour every day, filling the entire neighbourhood with

— صفحة 73 —

Stories of the Scholar

72

his hollering,, and even more so if he met the old man

accidentally in the street.

‘God help my father-in-law!’ he would call out, and use

every foul and dirty word to describe the gentle old man. He

cared nothing for the reputation of the family but continued

to shout obscenities in the street in the hearing of all the

passers-by. He threatened the sheikh… he threatened his

own wife… using the foulest language! He terrorised the

entire family so they could no longer go about their daily

lives and they became embittered by his undeserved cruelty.

And the poor sheikh trembled with fear and helplessness

because he knew of no way to escape from the man’s

malevolent onslaught.

Some people advised the sheikh to complain to the

authorities: he did so but it was no use! Certain intermediaries

intervened in this case and reported it to the French high

commissioner in Syria, but no help was forthcoming, for it is

well known that “nothing good can be expected from

someone who does not pray.”

Word came back from the high commissioner that as

the malevolent husband had not broken into the house or

caused any physical harm to the occupants he could not be

punished. This was the law and no action could be taken

against him.

But surely his daily verbal onslaught outside the sheikh’s

house and his intentions for the sheikh’s innocent daughter

should be considered a crime in itself! Eventually, due to

— صفحة 74 —

The False Penitent Will Never Succeed

73

continuous representation about this case the high commissioner

banished the man to Lebanon for just one month which was all

that could be done under French law.

The month went by and the damned offender returned.

Unfortunately the month in Lebanon had not helped him

to mend his ways, and he went back to shouting strings of

obscenities outside the sheikh’s house growing ever more

insistent and stubborn, even more wicked and ugly than

before the banishment. Daily he went to holler for the

return of his wife, issuing all manner of menacing threats if

the imam did not comply with his demands.

The family lived under a permanent cloud of anxiety and

terror, expecting that one day the husband might climb the

wall, sneak into the house, and kidnap his reluctant wife.

The sheikh would be powerless to stop him even though he

knew that his daughter would be carried off to be violated

and used to entertain the man’s low-life companions.

Days passed and still the criminal continued to act in this

manner that made the family’s life unbearable hell whereas

they used to be so happy. It was a hopeless situation as no-

one had the power or authority to stop him. Feeling utterly

helpless, with nowhere to turn for help, the sheikh could no

longer eat or drink, and sat alone out of sight of his family,

crying and begging God to save them from this evil,

despicable man, ‘Oh God… I’ve become terribly grieved and

it is You Who relieves… oh God… I’m powerless and You

are powerful… would You please turn this wicked man away

— صفحة 75 —

Stories of the Scholar

74

from us… drive him away please… and relieve us of his evil

in whatever way You wish.’

This poor sheikh went through a long period of harsh

cruelty during which he lost at least half of his weight

because he was unable to eat. After much suffering one of his

friends finally took steps to help him. He had heard of the

excellent reputation of Mohammad Emin Sheikho and his

great success in crushing crime and punishing criminals, so

he made it his business to speak to him about the matter of

the sheikh and his daughter. Mohammad Emin reassured

him with his heart-warming words, ‘Leave the matter to

me… and give good news to the sheikh that certainly the

problem will be solved with God’s Will… I shall ensure that

this devil divorces her willingly… or unwillingly…!’ Then he

invited the sheikh – the wife’s father – with two of his sheikh

brethrens to lunch the next day.

The sheikh could barely believe what he had heard and

said to himself, ‘Is it possible…? Will he really be able to

persuade that cursed villain to divorce her when the French

high commissioner failed to do so?’

As for Mohammad Emin, as soon as the sheikh’s friend

had left, he chose two of his most powerful and courageous

men from his band of reformed criminals… for he knew

the wrong doer (the sheikh’s son-in-law) since he had been

an officer in the army… but this criminal was not among

his men at the present time as he had not committed as

many serious crimes as Emin’s close criminal circle.

— صفحة 76 —

The False Penitent Will Never Succeed

75

He said to the two men, ‘Tomorrow, I want you to invite

the sheikh’s son-in-law to lunch at my house… tell him about

my invitation and bring him with you… is it understood?’

Then he revealed to them his plan to entrap the criminal

who was causing the family so much grief. The two men

answered, ‘Yes, sir… whatever you say!’

Next day, Mohammad Emin held a splendid banquet

where he offered the most magnificent and delicious food

and fruits. At lunch time the sheikh duly arrived with two

other sheikhs of his acquaintance and Mohammad Emin

welcomed them hospitably and showed them the respect

due to their status.

After a short time, the criminal, the subject of this tale,

arrived, and as soon as he entered the room and saw his father-

in-law, he stood at the door, ready to leave. Immediately he

said, ‘I won’t divorce my wife… I won’t…!’

Mohammad Emin said to him, ‘This is disgraceful…

did I ask you a question for you to speak like that? I simply

invited you to my house.’

But the wicked criminal took no notice of what he had

heard, and he continued, ‘I won’t divorce… I won’t…

otherwise, why is he here?’ and he pointed at his father-in-

law.

Our man replied to him in a way that would accept no

argument, ‘Did you hear me? Have I asked you to divorce

your wife so that you say such things?’

‘No,’ he replied.

— صفحة 77 —

Stories of the Scholar

76

Mohammad Emin said, ‘So why did you raise the

subject? He is a man who has respect for other men… go

into the room and sit down.’ Thereupon, he kept silent,

entered the room and sat down, still insisting that he would

not divorce his wife.

He soon composed himself and when Mohammad Emin

felt that he had calmed down, he got up and sat beside him

and then started to talk with him about divorcing his wife,

but unfortunately… he was rock-like in his obstinacy and

persistent in his hypocrisy… fully determined not to divorce

her.

Mohammad Emin then tried to tempt him by offering

him money… but he refused. There was still to be no

escape for that poor chaste woman.

By then, becoming increasingly annoyed he said to him

firmly, ‘So… you refuse to divorce!’

The wicked criminal replied, ‘That’s right… I will not

divorce her!’

He was about to learn that his time had run out!

Then Mohammad Emin decided to take action and gave

a simple pre-arranged signal to the two men from his

criminal band. No sooner had they received that signal

than they pounced upon the husband and grabbed his arm

forcefully, then they grasped him by the shoulders. He tried

to resist but he could no longer move as they were stronger

and braver than him and he knew that he had to give in.

Defiantly the criminal said, ‘Go on… kill me… I still

— صفحة 78 —

The False Penitent Will Never Succeed

77

won’t divorce her… so let a crime be committed in your

own house… oh Bey!’

He replied, ‘ No, I will not kill you… why should I bring

shame on my home?’ He then ordered his two men, ‘Strip

him… here… in front of the guests!’ The significance of this

act is that in the criminals’ code, the most disgraceful thing

that can happen is to be undressed before others, whereas to

murder someone is of very little consequence.

When the criminal heard our man’s order he lost his

mind, his inflexibility and tyranny were crushed, and he

was overcome and extremely humbled, then he shouted,

‘Oh sir… please… I seek refuge with you… I seek refuge in

your honour sir…’

Mohammad Emin replied, ‘You have no honour… you

vile individual!’ The two criminals set about stripping him,

then he shouted as if the world was closing in on him, ‘Sir,

please… I’ll divorce her… she is divorced… she is divorced…

she is divorced…’

At that moment Mohammad Emin called out to the

three sheikhs who were watching these events unfold. They

sat as though in a state of complete shock… that was

because when they heard the order to undress the criminal

they all shouted, ‘No… no…’ and the wife’s father cried

out, ‘I don’t want him to divorce her… let him go… I

don’t want him to divorce…!’

So, with these words from the sheikhs it seemed as

though he would be frustrated in the clever plan he had

— صفحة 79 —

Stories of the Scholar

78

thought up. But despite their strong objection he shouted

to his two men, ‘When you’ve finished with him do the

same with those three,’ and he pointed at the sheikhs.

The three sheikhs looked at Mohammad Emin in great

dismay, then they saw his face… he looked as fierce as a

lion and deadly serious; they were sure of what they had

heard but were so confused that they no longer had any

idea of what was going on.

But as the criminal repeated three times that he divorced

his wife, and added that the divorce was irrevocable,

Mohammad Emin wanted to make sure the three

bewildered sheikhs heard the oath of divorce, so he shouted

at them after shaking them with his hand in order to help

them to recover their wits and said to them, ‘Listen… listen

to what he’s saying.’ And when they became aware that he

was speaking, he said to the husband, ‘Repeat the oath of

divorce once more.’ Then the criminal said, not believing

that he would escape from the situation, ‘My wife is

divorced… divorced… divorced… I have divorced her

once and forever.’ And by that, he rejected his wife, and all

of them were witness to his words.

After that, Mohammad Emin – whose very appearance

could evoke terror in the hearts of even the most powerful of

men – addressed the two criminals from his band, ‘Listen to

me… let it be known to all villains that killing this dog is to

be considered a lawful action from this moment on… and

anyone who catches sight of him should kill him immediately.

Release this vile creature!’

— صفحة 80 —

The False Penitent Will Never Succeed

79

He fled the state of al-Sham and never returned, which

probably saved his life.

Then the other two criminals left after they had eaten

lunch and taken leave of their master. Mohammad Emin

addressed the three sheikhs, ‘Did you believe that I would

allow my men to carry out my order? It was no more than a

trick to make him agree to divorce… by God I would not

have allowed such a matter even if the woman were my

own daughter, but this malicious criminal and his likes do

not understand unless you speak to them in their own

rough language… and even if he had refused to divorce his

wife, I still would not have let such a thing happen at all…

and then I would have made a different plan in order to

force him to divorce her… but all that you have seen and

heard was just a ploy to save this poor woman from the

claws of this monster. At least I succeeded whereas the

French high commissioner failed.’

Thereupon, and after they heard his words, the three

sheikhs felt ashamed of their initial reaction, and they

looked at this merciful, humane thinker with their eyes full

of admiration and appreciation. Then they left Mohammad

Emin’s house, full of praise for him, and the father of the

young woman did not know how to thank this merciful

man and reciprocate his favour.

So he asked God to reward him in whatever way he

deserved. And surely, this is the best of all things!

chapters.title: صفحة 81 - 90 (The Minister of War Yusuf Al-’Azma and t)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 81 —

80

The Minister of War Yusuf Al-’Azma

and the Battle of Maysalun

e should open this account with a little

background history of that time when the

Ottoman Empire came to its end. The League

of Nations came into being after the end of World War

One: its task was to ensure that war never broke out again.

After the turmoil caused by the Versailles Treaty of 1918,

many looked to the League to bring stability to the world.

So, when the Ottoman Empire came to an end and had to

relinquish its authority over al-Sham and other countries,

an alternative authority was put in place to help those

countries through the transition. The Arab countries which

had recently separated from the Ottoman Empire were

considered to be underdeveloped and reactionary and should

be placed under a mandate in order to assist in their process

of civilisation and progress.

At a meeting of the Allied Powers in the Italian town of

San Remo a decision was taken under article 22 of the

covenant of the League of Nations to give France the

Mandate for Syria and Lebanon.

W

— صفحة 82 —

The Minister of War Yusuf Al-’Azma and the Battle of Maysalun

81

At that time, the king of Syria was Faisal ibn Sharif al-

Hussein who informed Britain of his government’s absolute

rejection of the decisions of the San Remo talks. On 14th

July in that same year, France was informed of the decision

of King Faisal and his government which prompted them

to send their interlocutors, General Gouraud and General

Allenby to enforce the decisions taken in San Remo. Hence

Gouraud sent a warning to King Faisal accusing him of

hampering the progress of the French forces by preventing

them from using the Riyaq-Aleppo railway line and he gave

him four days grace to comply with the following terms:

1

Hand over control of the Riyaq-Aleppo railway line

to the French.

2 Cancel conscription and disband the armed forces.

3 Accept the paper currency issued by France as the

legal currency.

4 Accept the French Mandate upon Syria.

Under the circumstances, the Syrian government was

compelled to accept these terms and informed the French

commissioner in Syria of their acceptance for this to be

transmitted to General Gouraud in Beirut. However, the

French had taken it upon themselves to disconnect the

telephone lines between Damascus and Beirut in the border

area of Serghaya in order to delay the Syrian government’s

approval from reaching General Gouraud. Hence, believing

the Syrians to be at fault General Gouraud ordered his

— صفحة 83 —

Stories of the Scholar

82

forces to march towards Damascus and Aleppo because of

the Syrian government’s apparent negligence. So, the forces

which presented in the north were ordered to move towards

Aleppo and those which were in Shtora were to march

towards Damascus. This occurred on July 23rd.

Meanwhile, and before this news reached the Syrian

government, they had actually set in motion the execution

of the articles of Gouraud’s caution, since King Faisal had

no choice. Given the difficult circumstances of the country

and its inability to defend itself against a state as powerful

as France, Syria’s acquiescence was inevitable.

At that time Yusuf al-’Azma was the minister of war.

When he was informed of General Gouraud’s military

advance to occupy Syria he issued a command that the

disbanding of the army should be halted immediately and

the soldiers who had been demobilized should be re-called.

He then gathered a force around him, armed them, and

took the decision to proceed towards Maysalun in order to

confront General Gouraud.

Through his military experience, minister Yusuf al-’Azma

was certain that the remainder of the army and a few young

volunteers would not be able to stop the French military

advance or repel it, so he might well leave, never to return;

that’s why he entrusted his only daughter Laila to a noble

Damascene family, by the name of al-Husari. He committed

her to Mr. Sati’ al-Husari’s care, saying to him, ‘I am leaving

my beloved daughter Laila entrusted to your care.’

— صفحة 84 —

The Minister of War Yusuf Al-’Azma and the Battle of Maysalun

83

As soon as he placed his beloved child under the custody

of Mr. al-Husari he went to the Royal Palace to ask

permission of King Faisal to advance on Maysalun; this was

granted. Then, Yusuf Bey, the minister, met with the retired

officer Mr. Mohammad al-Taghlibi, who accompanied him

to visit the venerable scholar Mr. Mohammad Emin Sheikho

before leaving for Maysalun.

In the house of the noble master, they were welcomed

most hospitably. Then, the three men sat discussing the

subject of the French military advance and the decision of

the minister of war, Yusuf al-’Azma.

The noble master could do nothing except advise him

saying, ‘Oh, Yusuf Bey! The weak are helpless in the face of

the mighty! You will face an army that is strong, well-

trained, highly disciplined and fully armed, which is surely

beyond your capacity. As you know, the region of Maysalun

is exposed from all directions and your going there means a

risk in the full sense of the word, and will lead you and all

the men entrusted to you to inevitable death… I advise you

not to go. You would do better to wait for the French here,

on the outskirts of Damascus. Surely, you know, Yusuf Bey,

that their only viable approach to Damascus is the al-Rabwa

corridor where they have no way but through a narrow

passage which runs between two mountains, so, when their

first tank arrives at the town of al-Rabwa , the last one would

just be reaching the beginning of the al-Rabwa corridor and

so all of their army would be enclosed within the passage. If

— صفحة 85 —

Stories of the Scholar

84

we position ourselves above them at the top of the

mountains on either side we could pound them with rocks

from above, and halt them in their tracks, trapped in the

narrow pass. Then, we can roll down huge rocks at the

beginning of the corridor from the Dummar side of the pass

and they will be trapped in the valley unable to advance or

retreat. Our men could then continue to heap rocks and

stones on them and open fire too. They would be defenceless

as their supply lines will be cut off, but we, on the other hand,

will still be able to get reinforcements of men and equipment

without being subjected to the danger of their fire.’

The minister of war, Yusuf al-’Azma, replied, ‘But Bey,

what will future generations have to say about us? They will

surely say that the citizens of Damascus are such cowards

that they put up no defence and waited till the French army

entered the city.’

The venerable master Mohammad Emin replied, ‘Oh,

Yusuf, Bey! This matter is of far greater importance than

any amount of talk or historical precedent… it concerns

the souls under our charge, and leading them there will be a

clear military error which will definitely result in failure and

death. The sound military logic in this situation calls for

our forces to wait for them at the al-Rabwa corridor and be

fully prepared to encircle them from above: preparing piles

of rocks as I have said, and setting up the sites and arsenal

of the fighters. And what’s more, with this strategy we can

ensure our supply lines.’

— صفحة 86 —

The Minister of War Yusuf Al-’Azma and the Battle of Maysalun

85

But, the minister of war refused to accept this sound

military logic, so he replied, ‘Oh Bey! I know perfectly well

that our victory will be impossible and death will be the

fate of most of my troops… yet, we have to confront them

so that the future generation cannot accuse us of cowardice

or say that we failed to go out to face our enemy but waited

till they were at the gates of our city… yes, we have to go…

otherwise history will record that General Gouraud met

with no resistance till he arrived in Damascus.’

Hence, the marks of sadness appeared clearly on the

features of the noble master whose heart is full of mercy, so,

he sighed deeply and then related the story of Abdul-

Mottalib, the grandfather of our master, Mohammad (cpth),

and his uncle Abu Talib. ‘Yusuf Bey,’ he said, ‘Please listen

to this story: when Abraha al-Habashi arrived in Mecca he

went to Abu Talib, after he had confiscated the camels of

Abdul-Mottalib. The latter went to meet him, and when

Abraha received him, Abdul-Mottalib accused him, saying,

“You have seized my camels and I want them back.” Abraha

said, “I thought you had come to dissuade me from entering

Mecca to defend it!” Abdul-Mottalib replied, “As for al-

Ka’ba, it has a Provider Who defends it.” Then, Abdul-

Mottalib took his camels, stood on a hill and said, “Oh,

Provider! I’ve guarded my own possessions, so, would You

protect Your Holy House?”

‘Therefore, you have to behave according to military

prudence and keep your men here so we can ask for their

help, and not go blindly towards an inescapable fate.’

— صفحة 87 —

Stories of the Scholar

86

But, alas! In spite of all this advice based upon wisdom

and relevant opinion, the minister of war did not agree

with the noble master, so he took leave of him and went

ahead with his men to Maysalun where he and most of his

men were martyred. The few who survived barely managed

to escape through the mountains.

Thus, Gouraud and his forces were able to enter Damascus

with relatively little opposition and he went to the shrine of

Salah al-Deen al-Ayubi, the leader of the Battle of Hattin

which had been fought many years before, and the liberator of

renowned Jerusalem, and there, he addressed the shrine

saying, ‘Rise… oh Salah al-Deen…! We are here again… we

have succeeded in occupying Syria!’

Many years passed after this sorry incident which caused

great heartbreak for the Syrian people. Then, a German

General came to General Abdullah Atfah who accompanied

him to visit the venerable master, Mohammad Emin

Sheikho, and there General Atfah spoke with him about the

story of the Battle of Maysalun: the arrival of the French

army in Syria, and about the plan which the noble master

had put forward, and through which the course of history

surely would have been altered.

When the German general had listened to the full details

of the ingenious plan that had been proposed by

Mohammad Emin he expressed his extreme admiration,

then he praised him saying, ‘Yes… exactly the apposite of

what happened and certainly the perfect tactic! Waiting for

— صفحة 88 —

The Minister of War Yusuf Al-’Azma and the Battle of Maysalun

87

the invading army in al-Rabwa would have been the right

stratagem, and it would then have been impossible for an

exhausted army coming from Lebanon to occupy Syria.’

— صفحة 89 —

88

The Tale of a Good Butcher

and a Bad Butcher

ne day, a butcher from the al-Midan district went

off to see Mr. Mohammad Emin in the district of

al-Muhajireen on Mount Qasiyun to rent a shop

from him. This was a shop that Mohammad Emin had

inherited, along with other property, from his father.

An argument had taken place between this butcher and

the inhabitants of al-Midan that prompted him to leave his

neighborhood and move to al-Muhajireen.

This butcher started to practise his trade in an open and

honest manner. He supplied his shop with only the best

carcasses: fattened young sheep with excellent, tender meat,

and he allowed the clients choose the cut of meat they

wanted, and let them choose which part of the carcass they

would like their meat from. It was usual for a customer to

want the choicest cut of meat which this butcher sold him

at the low price of the inferior cuts.

Even a child would be treated in the same fair way if he

came to buy meat for his family.

As a result, this butcher became widely-known throughout

the district and every day people would form a long, orderly

O

— صفحة 90 —

The Tale of a Good Butcher and a Bad Butcher

89

queue before his shop, each one waiting his turn irrespective

of their personal level in society. So, a typical scenario would

be of a senior officer standing in line behind a child, or a

simple workman.

Consequently, he sold many carcasses each day, and

with the high turnover his income was good though the

profit was small.

As for the leftover meat which was not fit for human

consumption, and the suet, he sold it wholesale to the

farmers who came to collect it every afternoon.

One day our man, Mohammad Emin, saw that a large

group of men had arrived from al-Midan and stood in front

of his shop greeting their former butcher and praising him

loudly. They had come to appease him and take him with

them after apologizing and soothing him for their previous

unseemly behaviour. He was happy to go along with this

genial crowd, so some of them set about collecting up the

tools of the butcher’s trade from the shop. Another group

hoisted him on to their shoulders to take him back to their

district… but the butcher shouted at them, saying, ‘Wait a

minute… I need to pay the rent to the shop owner.’ One of

them answered, ‘Don’t worry… I’ll pay him whatever he

asks.’

There and then, he headed for the shop owner,

Mohammad Emin, asked him how much rent was due, and

settled the amount in full.

And so, they went back to their own district with their

comrade carried high on their shoulders, clearly happy to

chapters.title: صفحة 91 - 100 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 91 —

Stories of the Scholar

90

be taking this excellent tradesman, a man of the highest

moral standing, back with them.

Some days later, another butcher came to rent the shop

from Mohammad Emin. He was completely different from

the first one: he was dishonest, he brought only the lowest

quality of carcasses to his shop; and if a child or a young

girl came to him, he would give them the worst piece of

meat he had and as a result, during the entire day he would

sell only half of the single carcass he had brought. His

dishonesty and the poor quality of his meat gradually led to

people avoiding him and going elsewhere to buy what they

needed.

That was what our man Mohammad Emin, the owner

of the shop, had noticed and as he was accustomed to doing

from the goodness of his heart, he wanted to advise the

butcher so that he might deal honestly with the clients and

provide them with good quality, tender meat. He explained

that the customers would be satisfied and buy greater

quantities of meat, and in turn he, the butcher, would gain

greater financial profit.

It was the sensible thing to do!

He said to the butcher, ‘Oh, brother, I see that your

business isn’t going very well, so I thought I should mention

to you that another butcher occupied this shop before you…

he brought only the best carcasses and best quality of meat.

For his honesty and fair treatment of his customers, Al’lah

made him very successful; all his carcasses were sold within a

— صفحة 92 —

The Tale of a Good Butcher and a Bad Butcher

91

few hours. It’s true that his profit on each carcass was quite

low because of his very reasonable prices but since he sold a

lot of meat every day his overall profit was very good. I

suggest that you should do as he did: bring only the best

kinds of meat, treat all of the customers fairly and make no

distinction between them! After all… the money of a rich

man has the same value as that of a workman!’

The following day, as our man was on his way to his

place of work, he looked at the shop and noticed that the

butcher had brought a carcass of good quality meat, so he

said to himself, ‘Thank God… he listened to my advice

and acted on it.’

But a great surprise was waiting for Mohammad Emin,

for when he left his work to go home, he passed by the

same shop and found the carcass still hanging as he had

seen it in the morning… still whole and not a single chunk

of meat cut from it. At the same time, the butcher was

wringing his hands in despair and raging against the man

who had advised him.

Mohammad Emin tried to pass without being noticed

by the cheating butcher but he could not go far as the

butcher’s shop was beside the door of our officer’s house

and he was waiting for him impatiently!

No sooner had he seen Mohammad Emin than he

intercepted him and blamed him for what had happened to

him after he had acted on his advice! ‘Look at the bad luck

you have brought me!’ he said in a quavering voice,

showing his anger and vexation.

— صفحة 93 —

Stories of the Scholar

92

Thereupon, Al’lah inspired Mohammad Emin to put his

hand on the butcher’s head and to say, ‘Swear by God and

His Envoy to tell the truth… didn’t you say to yourself, “If

I make a good profit I’ll continue to do business in the

correct way but if not, I’ll go back to my old ways and

bring bad carcasses and cheat the customers.”?’

At that moment, the butcher was flabbergasted that the

officer had seemingly read his thoughts. ‘How odd!’ he said

to himself. So, he asked him, ‘Who told you that? And how

could you know even though I didn’t voice my thoughts to

anyone?’

Then, our man answered him saying, ‘Go away… you

want to test your Provider; the Almighty should never be

tested… He should be obeyed and then, only then, you will

have good results.’

Having said this, Mohammad Emin went into his house

thinking about the matter of this stubborn butcher who

would not be able to sell any meat, and what a great loss he

would incur as a result!

After having his meal and taking a rest, he felt a certain

pity for him and went back to the shop and said, ‘Load

your carcass onto a mule and follow me.’

Our man took the butcher around to some of his

acquaintances who had restaurants and at Mohammad

Emin’s request each one of them bought a part of the

carcass so that the butcher regained his original financial

outlay; at least he managed to avoid what would have been

— صفحة 94 —

The Tale of a Good Butcher and a Bad Butcher

93

certain loss, because if the carcass had remained in his shop,

it would inevitably rot since there were no refrigerators to

keep food fresh at that time.

Next day, as our man was on the way to his place of

work he passed by the butcher’s shop as usual. Immediately

it became clear that some men will never learn the error of

their ways! He saw that the butcher had returned to his

previous habit of bringing an inferior quality of meat… and

his customers – who had similar bad characters – continued

to buy from him, “Impure men attract impure men, and

pure men attract men of purity.”

Really, the vicious spirits insisted on manifesting their

malice, and in the words of the proverb, “Like will always

attract like.”

— صفحة 95 —

94

The French Woman Learns

the Reason for the Veil

n the Holy Qur’an God says, “Oh Prophet, tell your

wives, your daughters, and the wives of true believers

to draw their outer garments over their bodies [when

outdoors], so they should not be known and not

molested. And Al’lah is All-Forgiving, All-Merciful.”

1

This is the Godly Law and divine Legislation which our

master, Mohammad (cpth), and all the Prophets and

Envoys (cptt) who came before him brought to mankind.

This Law leads to happiness which is the Purpose of this

Merciful and Tender Provider Who wants all His creatures

to enjoy happiness in this world and in the world to come.

But alas! Repulsive and devilish desires have made people

neglect these Laws. They did not stop to think! They

believed that their licentiousness way of life would bring

them happiness.

As for the man who is aware of the secret and the

wisdom of these Godly Laws and knows that people can be

1 e Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 33, The Combined Clans (al-Ahzab), verse 59.

I

— صفحة 96 —

The French Woman Learns the Reason for the Veil

95

pleased only when applying them, it is recognised that he

has true love for his Provider.

The closer and more loving a man is towards God, the

more understanding and knowledge of the Godly Purpose

behind His Statute he will acquire.

In order to clarify this, here is a story of an actual event

relating to a woman’s veil:

A meeting was held between the eminent scholar

Mohammad Emin Sheikho and a certain person of a high

social and cultural class. The man had gained a doctorate at a

time when there were no schools and the majority of people

were illiterate; education for those of a higher social rank

would be through tutoring. The meeting concerned some

details for the inauguration of Prince Abdul-majeed Haidar,

a king of Greater Syria at the time of the French mandate,

2

who had been approved by the French government to rule

the country.

On the following day at the time that had been previously

arranged, the eminent scholar, Mohammad Emin Sheikho,

went to that man’s house and knocked at the door. When he

realised that a woman had opened the door to him, he

turned his back on her. The woman was French and the wife

of the doctor, and being unable to speak Arabic she was

obliged to ask her daughter to explain that her husband

2 The French mandate of Syria was a League of Nations mandate created

after World War I when the Ottoman Empire was split by the Treaty of Sèvres.

— صفحة 97 —

Stories of the Scholar

96

would be ten minutes late because of an important meeting

with General Sarrail, the French resident in Syria. So, he

continued down the steps and waited in the street near the

house.

The doctor apologized for being late and our man

answered, ‘To be just ten minutes late is not considered late

at all!’

Then, they entered the house together and sat in the

salon. Before they began to discuss their business matters,

the doctor’s wife and their daughter came to join them at

the meeting. Mohammad Emin looked at her husband who

knew full well that he was not in the habit of sitting with

the fairer, gentle sex. The husband looked at his wife then

lowered his head and did not utter a word because he saw

that his wife’s face showed her intense anger.

She began to speak in French, with her daughter

translating her words into Arabic, ‘I believed in your

impeccable reputation, your international renown in

Lebanon. I valued you highly. Now I see that the opposite

is true.’

He was obliged to reply through her daughter, ‘Please

tell your mother that she is a fool.’

When she heard these abrupt words, she became agitated

and stood up crying out, ‘I’m a fool, am I?’

But one should remember, that it is well known that the

French have always been hot tempered.

He told her, ‘Of course you are. Anyone who gives two

completely contradictory opinions about a man whom he

— صفحة 98 —

The French Woman Learns the Reason for the Veil

97

does not know nor has ever met, is surely a fool. Have you

ever met me or even seen me before, that you can form

these two diverse judgements?’

She replied, ‘No; but why didn’t you come into the

house when I invited you? Am I not beautiful? My husband

knows that I am a charming Parisian woman! Have you

heard somewhere that I’m not an honest woman so that

you did not want to come in? Here is my husband, ask him

if he has found anything dishonest about me during my life

with him.’

Our man replied, ‘I am a Muslim. One of the basic

principles in our unquestionable jurisprudence is that men

keep to their own world and women keep to theirs. They

do not cross over… the social intermingling of men and

women is forbidden.’

She then said to him, in a most derogatory fashion, ‘You

Muslims have exaggerated so much. The Jews are older

than you are. The Christians are more powerful than you

are too. Where did you get this idea of the veil from?’

‘Is it a matter of age and power, or of logic, proof and

righteousness?’ our man asked.

She said, ‘Truly it’s a matter of evidence and proof.’

Clearly giving the matter some thought, Mohammad

Emin set out his reply with all seriousness, ‘So, let me show

the reason why Islam decrees that a woman should be

veiled in the presence of men. When I spend my time

talking and working with men, the harsher sex, all day long,

— صفحة 99 —

Stories of the Scholar

98

and then I come back home from work, the only woman I

see is my wife and for me she is the most beautiful woman

in the world. My love for her increases… the bonds

between us become stronger. This is very important for the

stability and emotional development of my children within

the family. When we sit together, it does not matter how

honest you and I are, and you certainly have charms and

excellent characteristics that possibly make you more

appealing than my wife. I may succumb to your charms

because I am a human being. When I return home, the

comparison will begin unconsciously between what I saw

and liked of those attributes which I do not find in my own

wife; then I’ll feel sorry for myself and my own bad fortune,

and think that my situation isn’t fair. I’ll ask myself why

this particular woman became my wife and not another

with greater charms or beauty! She does not possess the

same elegant beauty and charm as other women, nor is she

as articulate, or her voice as musical; she isn’t as attractive as

other women, nor does she have the same lightness of

soul… and I could mention even more. If these superior

qualities are presented to me they will likely lessen my love

for my wife and make me feel dissatisfied. Antagonism and

aversion will replace our previous feelings of love and

intimacy. When my wife is nice to me in her usual gentle

way saying ‘Oh my darling’, it will sound like a bullet

blasting my ears, because the feeling in my heart would

have changed.

— صفحة 100 —

The French Woman Learns the Reason for the Veil

99

‘ “God has not given a man two hearts”

3; so my love

for her will change as the spirit naturally tends towards the

most beautiful, the most charming, the most attractive and

the finest. Then, altercations will prevail instead of

cooperation, and injustice instead of justice. My wife may

put up with my bad treatment once or twice, but her

patience will soon come to an end. She will question herself

about the secret of this seemingly spontaneous reversal,

which is causing me to treat her in that way despite the fact

that she continues to do her duty towards me and my

children to the best of her ability. She will rebel and treat

me in the same fashion, and therein would lie the downfall

of our marriage. There would be tension in our relations.

Quarrels would begin for the silliest reason and tempers

would flare. Because of this change, life would become an

unbearable hell with divorce being the only solution. And it

wouldn’t be just the two of us who reap the result of

divorce, but it would be reflected upon the children.

Instantly they would lose their guardian, the person who

teaches them right from wrong; instead they would be

influenced by the misbehaviour of their friends in the

street, the place where they might well learn the arts of vice

and crime.

‘What’s more, my family and hers would become involved

in the quarrel too. This breakdown would extend further still

and have a very bad effect on the community. Due to the

3 e Holy Qur’an, Fortress (Surah) 33, The Combined Clans (al-Ahzab), verse 33.

chapters.title: صفحة 101 - 110 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 101 —

Stories of the Scholar

100

mingling of both sexes, and of women removing the veil, the

community becomes disconnected and it could easily be

destroyed. This would be the result of our mixing together;

despite the fact that both you and I are honest people.

‘This is from the man’s point of view. But in relation to

the woman, and through her meeting with a strange man,

she will like some characteristics in him such as the way he

talks, how he treats her, his outward appearance, his rank,

etc. She may not find these qualities in her husband. With

the passing of time her dissatisfaction with her husband will

grow, leading to antagonism towards her husband and the

beginning of disputes and quarrels.’

Then, Mohammad Emin looked at her and said, ‘If you

find good qualities in me… wouldn’t you like these

qualities to be available in your husband?’

She replied that she would like her husband to be the

best man in the world.

He continued, ‘Therefore, the absence of these qualities in

your husband would belittle him in your eyes, and his value

would decrease in your view. The only reason this might

happen is if you mix with men other than your husband. This

mingling would invariably lead you to like certain qualities in

other men, which are not found in your husband, and the

result would be feelings of disgust and repulsion instead of

love and enjoyment. Thus happiness is lost.’

When she heard this logical discussion as a positive

scientific analysis of a practical situation, she looked at her

— صفحة 102 —

The French Woman Learns the Reason for the Veil

101

daughter and said, ‘I want you to follow in the footsteps of

this man: become a Muslim like him, but not like your

father.’

Her husband, who had remained silent during this

conversation, bowed his head in shame because she was

aware of his behavioural practices that contradicted the

spirit of Islam.

After that the great eminent scholar took his leave of the

family and went home.

A few days later, the husband of the French woman

came to tell the honest master that his wife wanted to meet

him again for she had found in him true, meaningful and

logical words. He also intimated that she might have the

true desire to embrace Islam if she could meet him again.

Mohammad Emin apologised to her husband saying, ‘I

felt obliged to meet her the first time so as to reply to her

accusation of fanaticism within Islam regarding the use of

the veil and other matters. Now I do not want to go to

meet her of my own free will. The first time I saw her it was

through necessity and not by desire, but the second time

would be to meet her through my own conscious decision

and I may desire her… I am a human being, my brother…

thus I would bring ruin on myself and this is not

acceptable. If she wants to embrace Islam, that is her

choice, and should be made of her own free will.’

Less than a month later, the doctor returned to the

home of Mohammad Emin accompanied by his French

— صفحة 103 —

Stories of the Scholar

102

wife who was dressed in long clothes concealing her body,

and with her hair covered. The eminent scholar opened the

door for them although he was not expecting their visit. He

welcomed them and invited them to enter his house. When

they were seated comfortably in the salon she told him that

she had seen the Prophet Mohammad (cpth) in her sleep,

shining so brightly in his grandeur and beauty that all had

to avert their gaze: she had been shown the heavenly

delights of the sacred worlds and her spirit experienced a

beautiful paradise. She then came to loathe her base desires

and wanted nothing other than to reach that state of

transcendence. She added, ‘Since I had that great vision, I

began to live a life of fulfillment and enjoyment whereby

my emotional pain was changed into complete happiness.

And I’m still living that vision; for this reason I decided to

declare my conversion to Islam at your hands.’ And there

and then, she embraced Islam.

This true story occurred during the French Mandate

over Syria.

Then he added, ‘Once you embrace Islam you have to

cover your face in public in order to continue your life of

heightened spirituality, for we do not accept the feminine

charm that is harmful to man.’

She answered, ‘In all honesty I don’t feel that I can do it

yet because all my life I have been used to having my face

uncovered. So, I find it difficult to apply all of the

instructions at the same time.’

— صفحة 104 —

The French Woman Learns the Reason for the Veil

103

She asked him to be patient with her a little and

eventually she would accomplish that too in accordance

with God’s Will, and for her love of His Envoy (cpth).

The political troubles that stormed Damascus at that

time prevented them meeting again, but he was reassured of

her truthfulness. He was certain that she would accomplish

everything by God’s Will.

— صفحة 105 —

104

Defending the Sheikh against

a Murderous Mob

ohammad Emin Sheikho, the great humane

man, was devoted to a certain venerable sheikh

who was regarded by all with the highest

esteem. One day, the sheikh wanted to refurbish a room

inside the courtyard of Abu al-Nour Mosque in the Kurdish

region on the banks of the River Yazeed: a tributary of the

River Barada.

The engineers advised him that refurbishing the room

would be impossible unless the river could be diverted

temporarily for a few hours while the work was carried out.

So, having decided to go ahead with the project the sheikh

had the river diverted for just two hours, during which time

the work should be completed.

Yet many envious and evil men soon spread rumours

among the owners of the local fields, farmers and the

inhabitants of the region that Emin Kiftaro, the sheikh, had

arranged for the river to be diverted for the use and benefit

of his own followers, thus cutting off the supply from the

majority of people who relied on this water for their orchards

M

— صفحة 106 —

Defending the Sheikh against a Murderous Mob

105

and fields. This malicious story quickly spread widely among

the farmers like fire in a haystack. When it reached their ears

they did not stop to think, or ask questions, but rushed

around like mad men, calling on each other to attack and kill

the sheikh and to return the river to its original course.

They came from all directions carrying pickaxes, sticks

and such like, in order to attack the sheikh who was

innocent of any wrongdoing. Hundreds of men and youths

gathered in a great crowd, their numbers swelling to become

an overwhelming popular uprising as they approached the

sheikh’s house. They surged forwards aiming to storm and

burn the sheikh’s house, and kill him along with any of his

followers who might defend him.

When he saw the crowd approaching in the distance, the

sheikh became afraid for his life and was certain that he was

about to die: there was no way out for him, or anyone to

rescue him. The rabble were beyond wanting to hear the

truth about the diverting of “their” water and were hell-

bent on their mission, and he knew that he had no chance

of stopping them. So, he simply surrendered to the unruly

mob and what would surely be his impending death,

accompanied by four of his loving, faithful disciples who

resolved heart and soul to stand alongside him and meet

their end too, so that he should not face it alone.

In the meanwhile, during the last few minutes before the

mob would reach them, the dreadful news reached our

compassionate man, Mohammad Emin, while he was

— صفحة 107 —

Stories of the Scholar

106

coming along the same road, ‘Your sheikh has just been

killed!’ he was told.

No sooner had he heard those shocking words which had

come like a bolt from the blue, than he was stirred into

immediate action, like a predatory lion, and dashed quickly,

roaring and snarling, ‘I’m still alive, while my sheikh has

been killed… that should never have happened!’

He covered the distance in no time at all and when he

reached them, he saw the men and youths running towards

their prey yelling deafening, hostile threats. Over and over

they chanted, ‘Cut off our livelihood and we’ll cut off your

head! We want the soul of the man who’s deprived us of

our water,’ as they drew closer to his house.

As good fortune would have it they arrived there at the

same moment as Mohammad Emin Sheikho who turned to

face the murderous throng. Just then, a sound like the roar

of righteousness burst from him: a thunderous sound fell

on their ears as though a bomb had burst above their heads,

stopping them in their tracks.

This wide man began to heap insults upon them, describing

their malicious characters, and did not let up till their hearts

sank, their resolve weakened, and their fury abated; and when

he pounced upon them slashing left and right with his stick,

they were filled with horror and dread and scattered in every

direction, intent on escaping this terrible man. Now fearing for

their lives many of them tripped and fell, their feet unable to

bear them, and they felt as if death were about to overcome

them.

— صفحة 108 —

Defending the Sheikh against a Murderous Mob

107

Those hundreds of once brave men soon became terror-

stricken cowards and ran to hide wherever they could, behind

trees and the water wheels alongside the river: they could not

run fast enough from their attacker’s terrible wrath and

thunderous voice, which filled their hearts with absolute fear.

And yet, he continued chasing them like a raging lion, while

they failed to understand why they were overwhelmed with

such feelings of terror which was causing them to scatter in

every direction.

When the sheikh saw this man dashing towards the

throng and shouting at them he felt a sense of overwhelming

relief as he realised that the threat of death at the hands of

this terrible throng had been averted. As the horde scattered

in every direction the sheikh sent two of his disciples to

summon him.

Mohammad Emin entered his sheikh’s house, still in such

a state of extreme rage that he was like an erupting volcano;

his uproar did not subside for at least an hour, and his look

of fury could have reduced a towering mountain to dust.

There, his sheikh addressed him saying, ‘By the Almighty

God, when I saw you coming in that frenzied attack, I was

more afraid of your appearance than I was of my impending

death. So, I had to take my eyes off you, as I had never seen

such fury or awe-inspiring actions.

‘So! What is this great secret power encompassed in the

voice which Al’lah granted you?

— صفحة 109 —

Stories of the Scholar

108

‘What is that cloak of grandeur and veneration that

Al’lah has bestowed so lavishly upon you?

‘What is this great courage which excels that of all

others?

‘May God preserve and reward you for every act of

goodness, as He alone can reward you, not I!’

— صفحة 110 —

109

The Governor of the Castle Ensures

Stability within its Walls

hen Officer Mohammad Emin Sheikho was

named as governor of Damascus Castle and its

central prison, he became an object of envy for

all the other officers that worked there; for every one of them

aspired to that prominent position. Because of their jealousy

of him, some plotted together secretly to hatch a shocking

scheme whereby they sought to have him dishonourably

discharged.

Within days of taking up his new position Mohammad

Emin was quick to see the deceit and disloyalty in their eyes,

so he knew that sooner or later he would face many problems

and that he had to deal with them by careful thought and

intelligent planning. He felt that they were already conspiring

against him and frequently asked himself what it might be.

So, an air of suspense and vigilance infiltrated every corner of

the castle.

Officer Mohammad Emin looked around him surreptitiously,

constantly scrutinizing and studying all the officers and gendarmes

in the castle, yet he found none that he could trust and depend

W

chapters.title: صفحة 111 - 120 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 111 —

Stories of the Scholar

110

on, except for one simple, kind-hearted policeman. This man was

his aide who had been transferred with him to work alongside him

in the castle.

When Officer Sheikho sent for this policeman to come to

his office, he responded happily and immediately reported to

his superior; indeed he was in such a rush to respond to the

command that the cobblestones of the path resounded to the

footfall of his heavy boots.

‘Yes, sir!’ He saluted and greeted his commander eagerly

and with an air of great pride.

‘Welcome Abu Mohammad!’ our officer responded

kindly to his greeting, ‘Come in and have a seat… take a

rest.’

He sat with his face expressing his great pleasure because

of his true love and appreciation of his leader, the brave

officer.

Officer Mohammad Emin smiled, and then said to him,

‘Listen to me, Abu Mohammad. I want you to spread the

word throughout the citadel… among the gendarmes, the

officers and prisoners… that the new director of the castle

is an autocratic and tyrannical officer. Tell them that he

used to be the commandant of the commandos, and that’s

the reason the French government have assigned him to

this position. They wanted to use him to enforce discipline

and suffering on the Syrian prisoners. I want you to tell

them that he’s not in the least bit like any other officer and

that he has an iron fist that will kill anyone he strikes.’

— صفحة 112 —

The Governor of the Castle Ensures Stability within its Walls

111

Abu Mohammad’s eyes widened in wonder at what his

commander had just said. His features expressed both

astonishment and disapproval of what he had heard, so he

said, ‘God forbid! How can I say such things about you sir,

when your character is far above such autocratic and vicious

qualities? What you’re saying is a lie… there’s no truth in

it! You are the epitome of noble morality, compassion and

virility: you are really a gallant and honourable gentleman.’

‘Oh, you faithful man!’ our officer replied, ‘I’m asking

you to say exactly the opposite, and the more you

exaggerate in describing me as a cruel, hard-hearted man,

just as I’ve told you, the more you will help me tomorrow.’

Abu Mohammad complied with the order of his

commanding officer without questioning him any further,

and despite his amazement and confusion. He did not

understand why Officer Sheikho wanted this false story

about him to be circulated yet, by his commandant’s very

look and the tone of his voice, he sensed the seriousness of

the matter and that the desired outcome depended on his

success in achieving the orders of his master. Still confused

about the matter he nevertheless accepted to do as he had

been asked.

Abu Mohammad began to spread the false character

profile, as instructed, among the officers, gendarmes and

the prisoners, throughout the castle and its prison. Thus

everybody there heard of the apparent violence and cruelty

of the governor and that he was a man to be reckoned with

and should be regarded with awe.

— صفحة 113 —

Stories of the Scholar

112

Since our officer was always extremely earnest and had

gained the reputation of being as predatory as a lion, the

rumour quickly spread and was believed by many, but by

no means all, who heard it.

Despite that ingenious arrangement of Mohammad

Emin, there were still some inside the castle who persisted

in their erroneous ways and evil intentions. They made an

arrangement with their cronies to create some disruption

inside the castle and the prison so as to disturb the usual

state of controlled order, and spread chaos and confusion.

Such a situation would make it appear that he was

incompetent to hold such a high position and to be a leader

of so many men.

So, if their plot were to succeed, the French government

would then be obliged to remove him from his prominent

position of authority. That was the aim of these treacherous

officers and was exactly what our officer had anticipated

and was prepared for.

It was not long before several policemen burst through

the door of the commandant’s office, their faces ashen as

they gasped out, ‘Sir… sir, a prisoner in dungeon number

20, which is used for those sentenced to death, has stabbed

another prisoner. He was given a dagger secretly by a

corrupt gendarme, and now he’s standing there threatening

and menacing anyone who tries to approach him.’

Our officer gave them the order to arrest him but they

replied, ‘Sir, he may stab us if we approach him; so can we

shoot him and be done with it?’

— صفحة 114 —

The Governor of the Castle Ensures Stability within its Walls

113

Our officer realised immediately just what was going on!

They wanted him to give the order for them to kill the

criminal so it would seem that he was incapable of

controlling the prisoners, and he would then be responsible

for the murder of a prisoner. So, he was right in his initial

suspicions about them; for what he had expected was in the

process of becoming a reality.

He had told Abu Mohammad to spread a rumour about

his cruelty and violence around the castle only as an initial

arrangement. If this step failed to stop the deceit and the

conspiracy, it would be just the first basic stage of a plan to

prevent disorder, and impose order upon everybody in the

castle and its prison indefinitely.

Actually, the first precautions which he took did not

inhibit those envious officers from implementing such

actions. They had used one of their followers amongst the

gendarmes to give the criminal a knife which he used to stab

another prisoner. The injured man fell down bloodstained in

the middle of the dungeon; the other prisoners were shocked

and drew back towards the walls in fear for their lives, for

they did not know who his next victim might be. Then the

killer stood over the blood-stained prisoner, looking at him,

laughing hysterically, and clearly relishing the sight of the

blood and the groans of the dying man. The other prisoners

in the dungeon were not part of the plot, and did not realise

that the criminal had been given the dagger and instructed to

commit the crime, so that the director of the castle would

fall into a trap.

— صفحة 115 —

Stories of the Scholar

114

Officer Sheikho had been expecting the news and was

not in the least bit surprised, so he tackled the situation

immediately with firmness and resolve. He dismissed the

gendarmes angrily, and then he looked at Abu Mohammad

conveying by his look that he would deal harshly with those

who sought to disturb order and undermine his authority.

He said to him, ‘Abu Mohammad! You trusty and loyal

man! I want you to go straight to the dungeon and to tell

that criminal that the prison commander wants to see him

right now.’

‘But that’s impossible! How can you do that sir? Surely

he’ll refuse! He’s such a hardened criminal that he doesn’t

care about your orders.’

‘Don’t worry, you loyal man! Just give him my

message… I’m sure that he’ll refuse, so wait there for

exactly five minutes. And remember, don’t leave there until

I come to join you.’

Abu Mohammad saluted his commandant and hurried

away to carry out the order. He brought out a large key

from his waistband with which he opened the ancient iron

lock. The heavy door squeaked as it was opened and from

there he called out to the brutal criminal in a booming

voice, ‘Hey, you! The warden has ordered you to come to

his office at once.’

When the prisoner heard what Abu Mohammad said, he

started to laugh as though he were demented. Then he said

to him haughtily, ‘He wants me to go to him… me! Go to

— صفحة 116 —

The Governor of the Castle Ensures Stability within its Walls

115

him! What a joke! Does he really think that I’d do that?

How stupid!’

Then he began to swear at the warden in the foulest

language which demonstrated nothing other than his

contemptible behaviour and unbounded ignominy.

Abu Mohammad stood speechless beside the door,

waiting for his commandant as he had been ordered to do.

He was furious with the criminal but he controlled himself.

The prisoners wondered what was wrong with him! It was

not usual for a policeman to listen to that kind of abuse and

take no action. But the prisoners had no idea that Abu

Mohammad was simply obeying orders and they continued

to look at him while he remained on the spot for the five

minutes that the commandant had stipulated. They thought

that out of fear of his commander’s reaction if he failed to

obey the order, he did not move from his place.

Five long minutes passed before they heard the firm

footfall of our proud officer resounding on the stone floors.

He was drawn up to his full height and entered the cell with

sparkling eyes, a sword and two revolvers hanging from his

belt. He halted before all the prisoners, and stood there as

solid as a rock. His appearance was truly awe-inspiring.

Then, like a clap of thunder his voice reverberated off the

solid stone walls and addressed the gendarme, Abu

Mohammad, ‘Woe betide you! Didn’t I tell you to fetch that

cowardly dog to me at once? How dare you disobey my

order?’

— صفحة 117 —

Stories of the Scholar

116

Then, as quick as lightning, he slapped him so forcefully

that he landed face down on the ground two metres away

with bloodstained lips.

It was such a terrible shock for Abu Mohammad that it

left him speechless and stunned… unable to move. He

remained where he was, lying on the floor, stupefied more

by the emotional shock than the physical one. He could not

believe what had happened… one moment he was carrying

out the commandant’s order… and the next moment that

same commandant that he held in such high esteem, had

knocked him to the ground for no apparent reason.

Silence prevailed; astonishment and surprise could be seen

on the face of every man present, both prisoners and

gendarmes alike! The warden’s action was shocking! The

common military tradition of that time considered the

public denigration of a gendarme as an atrocity for whatever

reason it was carried out; how would they then regard this

beating of the gendarme by his commanding officer?

All present then understood the reality of what they had

heard of his character and became sure of its truth when

they witnessed that unexpected event.

‘If Abu Mohammad, the gendarme, had been treated in

that way simply because of his delay in carrying out orders,

although it was not his fault, what would be the

punishment of a prisoner in the castle – who deserves to be

punished – if he disobeyed orders? So, what we heard about

his tyranny and cruelty is true. His strike leads to the grave

— صفحة 118 —

The Governor of the Castle Ensures Stability within its Walls

117

and none can escape from him when disobeying orders. He

does not care for laws or traditions. Definitely, the

government has given him a free hand. Really, he seems to

be the cruellest of commandants; so God help anyone who

disobeys his order.’

These were the thoughts running through the minds of all

the prisoners who had witnessed this event. At that moment, a

terrible silence spread over the place because of the enormity

of the event which had left everyone dumbfounded. All of

them were totally shocked at what they had seen, and

overwhelmed by alarm and fear.

All the while Mohammad Emin was not looking directly

at the criminal, but he could see him from the corner of his

eye and was aware of his every movement.

Again, his voice resounded around the dungeon like a

thunderclap, as he ordered the prisoners to leave the cell.

They were trembling and all obeyed without hesitation,

starting to file out one by one.

In the meantime, some of the criminal’s cronies gave a

sign to him to drop the dagger and to mingle among the

rank and file of the prisoners to save himself from our awe-

inspiring officer. Yet nothing escaped the keen eyesight and

acuity of Officer Sheikho, who was covertly following the

villain’s every movement, before and after he threw down

the dagger. The criminal managed to mingle among the

crowd until his turn came to file out. As soon as he had

taken a couple of steps past Mohammad Emin, our officer

— صفحة 119 —

Stories of the Scholar

118

fell into line behind him like his shadow, then in a flash he

stretched his leg forward and hooked it in front of the

criminal’s legs; their momentum carried them forward so

they were now locked together. At the same time, his hand

landed firmly in the middle of the criminal’s back… and

crash… he was lying full length on the floor.

‘Oh God! Is this human strength? It’s more like

superhuman power,’ the prisoners said to one another in

astonishment. ‘Oh God! What a brave man!’ they said

secretly to themselves.

They had not noticed the officer’s legs interlocking with

those of the criminal, causing him to fall flat on his face.

They thought it was only that terrible blow which had

caused the criminal to fall so heavily. Then, our officer set

about beating and kicking him until he had beaten him

senseless. There, he called upon the scheming gendarmes

and ordered them to drag the criminal by his legs and

throw him into solitary confinement.

Fear and alarm spread throughout the castle after details

of the incident circulated, and everybody there became

panic-stricken. They all knew for certain that anybody

falling foul of the strong arm of the new director would

surely be destroyed.

Officer Mohammad Emin did not stop there! In his

determination to restore his authority he took further steps

and visited every cell in the prison. Some of those cells were

large enough to hold almost a hundred prisoners. There,

— صفحة 120 —

The Governor of the Castle Ensures Stability within its Walls

119

the officer of imposing stature began to pace and roar

throughout the large space. He removed his badges, then

rolled up his sleeves and turned towards the crowded

prisoners with a determined face like a lion on the prowl.

‘Come on, men,’ he said, ‘let’s forget about military

regulations! It’s well known that most prisoners are honest

heroes (although he knew that was not true!). Now, I’m

taking off my badge so we can romp together, man to man,

in sportsmanship. I promise that if any one of you can

withstand just one blow of my arm without falling over, I’ll

give that man a privilege over all the other prisoners. I will

let him move freely wherever he wants around the castle all

day long; I’ll also shower him with hospitality and gifts. So,

is there anyone here that wants to accept the challenge?’

Everybody heard that tempting challenge, but they were

all cowed by what they had seen and heard. Not a single

one of them dared to accept Officer Sheikho’s challenge,

for his stature and vehemence had really terrorized and

shocked them. So, through his exceptional wisdom and

mastery his plan stopped the plot in its tracks! After that

event, everybody in the castle, officers, gendarmes and

prisoners, submitted to him. Security and order prevailed

and Mohammad Emin ensured that they remained in

constant awe of him.

But what about Abu Mohammad?

When our officer finished quelling the problem in the

prison, he sent for him to come to his office.

chapters.title: صفحة 121 - 130 (Stories of the Scholar)
chapters.html:
— صفحة 121 —

Stories of the Scholar

120

Poor Abu Mohammad! He came into the office in a

terrible state. He was so sad and broken-hearted that he was

barely able to speak, but thoughts were flying around his

mind, ‘I can’t believe what happened! It is me, sir… it is

me who loves you… who serves you faithfully and

wholeheartedly… who has never broken even one of your

orders! Oh sir… I can’t understand why you did that to

me, sir!’

But our officer broke into his thoughts with a voice full

of tenderness, mercy and kindness, ‘Naturally, you’re upset

at what happened!’

Abu Mohammad did not answer.

‘Oh my brother,’ our officer continued in the same

gentle tone which overwhelmed him with love. ‘Both you

and I were about to fall into a dangerous trap and inevitable

disaster; so to avoid that danger and put an end to the

impending sedition in the castle and, too, because of the

craftiness and spite of the officers who tried to discredit me

I was obliged to do what I did.’

Our man kept talking to Abu Mohammad in a friendly

way until he made him forget all his bad feelings. Then he

brought out two golden liras from his pocket and gave

them to him, moreover he gave him one month’s leave with

his salary fully paid.

Abu Mohammad opened his eyes and showed his

pleasure and satisfaction. His lively voice clearly expressing

his renewed high spirits and delight, ‘If that’s how it is sir,

— صفحة 122 —

The Governor of the Castle Ensures Stability within its Walls

121

then beat me again and give me more golden liras and more

leave.’

Our shrewd officer laughed, and there and then Abu

Mohammad saluted him and left the officer with a spring

in his step.

And so, everything turned out for the best in the castle

by virtue of the brilliant conduct of our officer: security and

peace prevailed within its walls, and remained thus all

during Officer Sheikho’s administration of its affairs.

— صفحة 123 —

122

Occasional Marital Privacy for Prisoners

ere we tell of another incident during the

illustrious career of Officer Emin Sheikho which

is quite different from any of his daring military

escapades, and demonstrates a most humane side of his

character.

When he held the post of manager of the citadel prison

in Damascus it was customary for family and friends to visit

the prisoners on a particular day. On this day, he ordered

the prison warders to allow the prisoners’ wives to meet

with their husbands privately, for a limited time, in

individual rooms. There was no provision made in prison

regulations for this relaxing of the rules so the warders

disapproved of this move and were extremely resentful to

carry out this order. They considered that guarding the

prisoners while they were alone with their wives was outside

their field of duty and detracted from their own dignity.

Not to be outdone, that noble man, the great officer,

took up a firearm and assumed the duty of the simple guard

in front of the individual prison rooms which he had
